item.title: Swiss paycheck 2026: guide for single border workers
item.description: AVS/AI 5.3%, AD/AC 1.1% and LAMal: what to check in the paycheck of a single border crossing in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%; AD/AC 1.1% - Elderly: exemption €7,500 in the 2024–2033 scheme - New frontier workers: deductible €10,000
## Key facts - Signing of the New Cross-border Workers Agreement → 23 December 2020 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Withholding tax on earned income → only in Switzerland - Convention against double taxation → 9 March 1976 - AD/AC → 1.1%, with cap CHF 148'200 - LPP → 7–18% by age group, from 25th year - Italian IRPEF 2026 → 23%, 33%, 43% - KVG → health insurance
On 1 January 2024, the New Cross-border Workers Agreement came into force, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. For the cross-border worker who checks his Swiss pay slip in the Canton of Ticino in 2026, this sequence is the starting point: the reference is not an agreement that came into force in 2026, but a regulation that is already operational.
The tax principle is clearly defined: the cross-border worker's income is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit to be indicated in the EC framework of 730. It is therefore not a double withholding tax on the same income. The Italy-Switzerland Convention on double taxation was signed on 9 March 1976; Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA.
To read the payslip as a single person, it is best to separate the tax part from the social items. Withholding tax rates, including federal and cantonal ones, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At the federal level, administration is the responsibility of AFC/ESTV; at the cantonal level, the cantonal tax administrations intervene. UFAS and BFS do not set these rates: the first concerns social security, AVS/AI, while the second collects statistical data.
### The dates that separate the regimes
The operational distinction concerns the date of 17 July 2023. Old cross-border workers, already cross-border workers before that day, have the exemption of €7,500 in the transitional regime 2024–2033. New cross-border commuters are included in the €10,000 exemption. The distinction precedes any reading of the net: before attributing a result to the condition of being single, one must place oneself in the correct category.
The Italian picture changes from 2026. For the Italian IRPEF three bands are indicated: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. For incomes 2024–2025 the reference remains 23%, 35%, 43%. The modification is referred to in Law 199/2025, article 1, paragraph 3.
Finally, the G permit, the AVS and the LPP enter into the pay slip control; for health coverage the correct term is KVG, i.e. health insurance, not "health tax". The new 2026 tax agreement must therefore be placed in the actual chronology: the New Cross-border Agreement operates from 1 January 2024. ## From gross to items that reduce net
The Swiss paycheck for 2026 cannot be interpreted with a single percentage. For a single cross-border commuter, the useful check is to combine the tax withholding with the contribution items and health coverage, without adding amounts that belong to different plans. The table collects the values ​​indicated for the employee or for the relevant contribution item.
### Two comparisons to make before looking at the net
| Voice | Indicated value | How to read it | |---|---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% employee | social contribution | | AD/AC | 1.1%, cap CHF 148'200 | contribution with indicated ceiling | | LAINF | 0.7–1.5% | indicated rate | | BVG | 7–18% by age group, from age 25 | data related to age | | KVG | right of option for cross-border workers G; adult deductibles CHF 300–2'500 | health insurance |
The first scenario concerns a cross-border worker who was already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023: in comparison with the new regime, the data to highlight is the exemption of €7,500, valid in the transitional period 2024–2033. The second concerns a new cross-border worker: the threshold to be compared is the deductible of €10,000. They are two different readings of the same pay slip and should not be merged into an average.
The IRPEF calendar must also be kept separate. From 2026 the bands indicated are 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000 and 43% above; for 2024–2025 they are 23%, 35%, 43%. These percentages describe the Italian situation and do not transform the Swiss withholding into a second income tax: the mechanism indicated remains the tax credit of the EC framework of 730.
For singles, the practical point is not to confuse the KVG item with the other deductions. A cross-border worker with a G permit has the right of option; the source also indicates deductibles for adults from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. The deductible should not be transcribed as a salary rate: it is the health parameter reported for health insurance.
The real net therefore emerges from the separate reading of tax, AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF, LPP and KVG, not from the use of an indistinct total. To transform this grid into a personalized salary estimate you can use calcolatore fiscale, keeping the Italian tax part separate from the Swiss one. ## Operational checklist for 2026
Paycheck verification does not require starting from a theoretical figure. It requires classifying each item and linking it to the correct regime. For single cross-border commuters, the following sequence helps to avoid confusing entry date, withholdings and health coverage.
### Five checks on the payslip
1. Identify the regime. Note if you were already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023. The answer addresses the comparison between the €7,500 exemption in the 2024–2033 transitional regime and the €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers.
2. Isolate the tax. Search for the withholding tax on earned income and check the principle applied: for cross-border workers it is only in Switzerland. For the Italian side, the tax credit passes through the EC framework of 730, so the control remains consistent with the rule against double taxation.
3. Read the contributions one at a time. AVS/AI/IPG is 5.3% dependent; AD/AC is 1.1% with cap CHF 148'200; UVG is 0.7–1.5%; LPP is 7–18% per age group from 25th year. Do not replace one entry with another.
4. Separate healthcare. KVG means health insurance. If you are a G cross-border commuter, consider the right of option and the adult deductible between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500. The healthcare item must be read separately from social security.
5. Attribute responsibility. For federal and cantonal rates, the administrative reference is AFC/ESTV at federal level and the cantonal tax administration at cantonal level. UFAS does not set tax rates and BFS collects statistical data.
This grid also avoids confusing the envelope entries with other references to cross-border work, such as refunds, INPS or the Brogeda crossing. None of these terms replace the AVS, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP rates, nor change the principle of withholding tax. The same caution applies to the new 2026 tax agreement: the date to be verified remains 1 January 2024, not 2026.
To estimate the real net, enter in the reading only the values actually available on the pay slip and apply the 2026 calendar to the Italian IRPEF: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. For a working estimate of net, use simulatore busta paga.

item.title: Lugano human rights film festival: the best film is promised spaces
item.description: Best Film Winner: Ivan Markovic's Promised Spaces NGO Award for Effondrement of Anat Even Audience Award for Trop c 'est trop by Elisé
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Best Film Winner: Promised Spaces by Ivan Markovic - NGO Award assigned to Effondrement by Anat Even - Audience Award to Trop c'est trop by Elisé Sawasawa ## Key facts - Festival: Human Rights Film Festival Lugano - Winning work: Promised Spaces - Winning director: Ivan Markovic - NGO Award: Effondrement (Collapse) - NGO Award director: Anat Even - Audience Award: Trop c'est trop - Audience Award director: Elisé Sawasawa
The award ceremony of the Human Rights Film Festival Lugano has taken place, a prominent cultural event that saw the triumph of films committed to social, geopolitical and environmental themes. The main work that won the recognition as Best Film is 'Promised Spaces' by Ivan Markovic, a cinematographic work positioned halfway between fiction and documentary and set in contemporary Cambodia. The official jury that decreed the victory was composed of producer Gudula Meinzolt, active between Switzerland and Germany, film curator and programmer Dimitris Kerkinos, from Greece, and director Robin Petré, originally from Denmark. The jury expressed a detailed motivation to award the feature film, emphasizing how the work manages to create an extraordinary atmosphere of a dystopian society. The film addresses with great mastery the clash between different contexts and social classes, proposing itself as a hybrid work capable of inviting the viewer to a deep reflection on the current state of human relations, without imposing unambiguous or simplistic messages. The film also prompts consideration of how human action interferes with nature, transforming entire ecosystems into places rendered unrecognizable. The aspects of alienation that run through the entire visual narrative are further reinforced by a particularly careful and rigorous compositional and visual approach. For enthusiasts wishing to catch up on the viewing, the film is scheduled for a rerun at Cinema Iride. The cultural event continues to represent an important point of reference for the debate on human rights and major global issues within the Ticino city and regional context, attracting audiences and industry professionals from various regions and offering an international showcase for documentary and fiction cinema committed to addressing the most urgent and complex contemporary social issues. Alongside the main award assigned to Ivan Markovic, the jury and partner organizations of the festival have conferred other important official prizes that enrich the balance of this edition of the Lugano film event. The prestigious NGO Award was assigned to the work 'Effondrement' (Collapse), a film directed by Anat Even. Once again for this edition, the recognition was granted with the support and participation of Amnesty International Switzerland. The jury tasked with evaluating the works for this specific section was composed of Larissa Mettler, acting as co-president of the Executive Committee of Amnesty International Switzerland, alongside RSI journalist Moira Bubola and historian and journalist Jean-Marie Banderet. The official motivation released by the jury emphasizes how the voices and images within the film blend together in a way similar to the pieces of a puzzle, uniting different experiences and perspectives to bear witness to the moral collapse of a society at the moment when its own army carries out an action of systematic annihilation. The film was shot near the Gaza Strip after the date of October 7, 2023, capturing the remains of the kibbutz of Nir Oz, from which the population had been evacuated, and the destruction of the region beyond the border, with the aim of telling the story of the profound trauma generated by war and violence. A rerun screening is also scheduled for 'Effondrement' at Cinema Iride, thus offering a further viewing opportunity to the public interested in the international geopolitical and humanitarian themes addressed by the festival. The Lugano event also paid great attention to the feedback and direct participation of spectators, culminating in the awarding of the Audience Award. This recognition went to the work entitled 'Trop c 'est trop', a film made by director Elisé Sawasawa. The film focuses its attention and narrative on the ongoing armed conflict in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, documenting in particular the dramatic events related to the fall of Goma. The choice of the public confirms the sensitivity of the festival's spectators towards the humanitarian crises that are less told by the mainstream media but of dramatic global relevance. The programming of the Lugano Human Rights Film Festival is therefore confirmed as a central moment of cultural deepening, offering through screenings and debates with directors and experts a unique opportunity to discuss fundamental rights, the protection of natural ecosystems and the documentation of contemporary conflicts. The exhibition, through its different competitive and informative sections, continues to consolidate its role in the Ticino cultural scene, enhancing cinema as a tool for social investigation, historical testimony and promotion of civil and international awareness.

item.description: The Sharks win the Cup derby in Trevano Bissone goes down 25-14 Veljko Krstic scores six goals on his official debut Alfano scores five goals Location
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Sharks win the Cup derby in Trevano - Bissone surrender 25-14 - Veljko Krstic scores six goals on his official debut - Alfano scores five goals
## Key facts - Place → Trevano - Competition → Swiss Cup - Result → 25-14 - Coach of Lugano → Federico Pagani - New signing → Veljko Krstic - Krstic Networks → 6 - Alfano networks → 5 - Next opponent → St. Gallen
On Thursday evening, in Trevano, the Lugano Sharks won the Swiss Cup derby against Bissone, the home team led by Mihalov. The match ended at 25-14 and gave Federico Pagani the best possible start on the Lugano Sharks bench.
### Sharks night
Bissone sold their lives dearly before surrendering to their more esteemed opponents. The derby belongs to those challenges in which the difference in category traditionally struggles to emerge, because both teams face the match with particular passion or pressure. In Trevano this characteristic accompanied a game that remained open before the guests broke away.
The home team started in front, while the Sharks needed to gradually take control of the match. When Lugano imposed its greater experience and quality, the result began to shift in favor of Pagani's team. Bissone, however, had another jolt at the beginning of the third period, confirming the resistance shown in the match.
For Pagani it was the first official outing at the helm of the group. His debut as coach of the Lugano Sharks thus coincided with a victory in a Swiss Cup derby, at the end of a match in which Mihalov's team succumbed only after putting their opponents in the position of having to build the success during the match.
The 25-14 closed Trevano's evening and opened Pagani's adventure in the way described by the news: with a victory against Bissone and with an overall performance judged to be worthy of the commitment. The Swiss Cup now leaves room for the next appointment already indicated for the Sharks. ### The match changes gear
The first period saw Bissone slightly ahead. Mihalov's side therefore made a favorable start at home, while the Sharks had to wait until the next phase to take control of the contest. From that moment on, the Lugano team took charge of the match and made their greater experience and quality count.
| Phase | Progression | |---|---| | First period | Bissone slightly ahead | | Start of the third period | Surge from Mihalov's players | | Final phase | The Sharks finally pull away |
Bissone's reaction also came at the beginning of the third period. Mihalov's players had another surge, but the push was not enough to prevent their opponents from extending their lead. The final phase can be attributed to two elements evident in the reconstruction of the match: on the one hand, the tiredness of Bissone's most representative players, and on the other, the Sharks' bench, which was longer and more experienced.
The individual statistics gave a clear shape to Lugano's performance. On his first official appearance, Serbian newcomer Veljko Krstic immediately demonstrated his value, recording six goals. Right behind him was prolific scorer Alfano, with five goals.
However, the numbers of the two scorers do not tell the whole story of the evening. Coach Federico Pagani's team proved up to the task as a whole, managing the transition from the opening phase, which favored Bissone, to the part of the match in which the Sharks imposed their quality.
The match also marked Pagani's official debut after the change on the bench. The new coach took over from Jonathan Del Galdo, an experienced Genoese coach who had been in charge of the group for the last four seasons. The victory in Trevano thus marked the first official outing for both the new coach and the Serbian signing for Lugano. ### The next fixture
With the Swiss Cup challenge now behind them, the Sharks' schedule already features a new commitment. The Lugano team will return to the water tonight at the Lido pool, where they will host St. Gallen in the opening match of the Swiss Trophy.
The transition from Trevano to the Lido marks the change in venue indicated by recent events: moving from the derby against Bissone to the opening match of another tournament. St. Gallen will be the opponent in the first Swiss Trophy match, with the Sharks called upon to dive back into the action shortly after their victory in the Swiss Cup.
The competition has a specific characteristic. The Swiss Trophy is in fact a tournament dedicated solely to Swiss players or players who developed their athletic careers in our country. This definition distinguishes this upcoming commitment from the Cup match played in Trevano and clarifies the scope of the event.
For Lugano Sharks, the fixture at the Lido pool comes after Federico Pagani's official debut on the bench and the performance of new signing Veljko Krstic. The source presents the match against St. Gallen as the inaugural one, without indicating other tournament results or further stages of the calendar.
The next match will therefore be played at home, with Lugano called to host St. Gallen. The evening at the Lido completes the immediate aftermath of the Swiss Cup derby and brings the Sharks back into the water for the start of the Swiss Trophy, the tournament reserved for Swiss players or those who grew up athletically in the country.

## TL;DR - Lugano challenge Pully on Sunday at 2pm. - The Tavern hosts the Young Boys at 4pm. - Four teams are already in the third round. - Lugano and Taverne are the Ticinese still in the running.
## Key facts - Swiss → Cup Competition - Lugano → Pully Challenge, Sunday at 2 pm - → Young Boys Tavern Challenge, Sunday at 4pm - Campo del Taverne → Comunale - Ranking of Taverns → second in Group 3 of the First League - → Second Interregional League Pully Category - First-qualified → Stade Lausanne, St. Gallen, Servette and Basel
TAVERNS - The first knockout weekend of the Swiss Cup left two Ticino teams in the running: Lugano and Taverns. Mattia Croci-Torti's men will face the Pully on Sunday at 2 pm. The Carbone line-up, on the other hand, will host the Young Boys at 4 pm at the Comunale.
The double appointment offers two very different scenarios. Lugano comes to the confrontation after the success obtained in the debut of the Conference League and starts as an absolute favorite against Pully. The Vodese team will be able to count on enthusiasm and fans, but the technical distance from the Bianconeri is indicated as very wide. Pully plays in the Second Interregional League and, against Lugano, indicated as the strongest formation in the country at this stage, starts without the favours of the forecast.
For the Tavern the task is the opposite. The home team is second in Group 3 of the First League and will try to surprise the Young Boys, one of the nobles of national football. The goal indicated for the Ticino training is access to the round of 16, but to achieve this, an enterprise will be needed. The comparison then puts in front of a team that starts with a clear advantage in the evaluations and another call to try the surprise.
The schedules separate the two matches, but the meaning for the Ticinese is the same: to continue the path in the Swiss Cup after the first knockout weekend. Lugano seeks passage to the third round; Taverne must instead overcome one of the most emblazoned opponents in national football. The double commitment thus assigns the Bianconeri the role of favourites and the Carbon team that of possible surprise. The qualification picture opened with four results already decided. Stade Lausanne, St. Gallen, Servette, and Basel are the first teams to have reached the third round. Their results were as follows:
| Team | Result | Opponent | |---|---:|---| | Stade Lausanne | 2-0 | Étoile Carouge | | St. Gallen | 2-0 | Rapperswil | | Servette | 4-0 | Rotkreuz | | Basel | 3-0 | Stade Nyonnais |
These results leave Lugano and Taverne as the only Ticino survivors from the first weekend. For the two cantonal teams, therefore, the verdict has yet to arrive. Pully is described as a Vaud side backed by enthusiasm and fans, but coming from the Second League Interregional. Taverne, on the other hand, enter as runners-up in Group 3 of the First League and face Young Boys.
The contrast between the two matchups also concerns the predictions. For Lugano, the technical level of the bianconeri makes the match largely favorable on paper. For Taverne, the challenge at the Comunale is a much sterner test, because on the other side is one of the aristocrats of national football. In both cases, however, the objective remains qualification for the third round of the Swiss Cup, the goal toward which the two remaining Ticino sides are looking.
The sequence of results already decided adds a precise reference to the day: four teams have completed their commitments with margins of two, three, or four goals, while Lugano and Taverne still have to play their respective matches. The picture of the first qualified teams is therefore already defined, but the path of the two Ticino formations remains to be decided on the pitch. The rest of the weekend is focused on Sunday's two matches. At 2:00 PM, Lugano will face Pully. The immediate precedent is their success in their Conference League debut, a factor that accompanies Mattia Croci-Torti's team toward a match in which they are considered the absolute favorites. On the other side, there will be a team from Vaud driven by enthusiasm and fans, but seen as far from the technical level of the 'bianconeri'.
At 4:00 PM, it will be Taverne's turn at the Comunale. To advance to the round of 16, Sabbatini and his teammates must first hope that Gerardo Seoane's team takes the field without maximum determination and focus. This possibility must be followed by a classic perfect performance from the home side. These are the necessary steps to try and overcome one of the elite clubs of national football.
The chances of success for Taverne are described as low, but not zero. The possibility remains open because, in the recent past, the team has already shown several times that it can surprise. The difficulty of the challenge remains high and depends on the ability to exploit any potential lack of motivation from Young Boys and to deliver the perfect match required of the Ticino team.
For the two Ticino teams, the schedule leads to a different verdict to be built on the pitch. Lugano aims for the third round starting from a position of clear advantage; Taverne, on the other hand, is looking for a performance that can turn a slim chance into qualification. Sunday's matches at 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM will be the next step in their Swiss Cup journey.

item.description: Three Valli Varesine seventh in the ProCyclingStats ranking The race scored 913 points Liège, Vuelta and Paris-Roubaix are behind The Tour de France
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Tre Valli Varesine seventh in the ProCyclingStats ranking - The trip scored 913 points - Liège, Vuelta and Paris-Roubaix are behind - The Tour de France drives with 1567 points ## Key facts - Competition → Tre Valli Varesine - Portal → ProCyclingStats (Pcs) - Position → seventh place - Score → 913 points - Liège-Bastogne-Liège → eighth place - The Vuelta a España → ninth place - Paris-Roubaix → eleventh place - First place → Tour de France, 1567 points ### Seventh place in the Three Valleys With 913 points, Tre Valli Varesine achieved seventh place in the ProCyclingStats ranking, a portal specialized in evaluating races through a scoring system linked to the ranking of participants. The historic race in the Varese area thus confirms itself as a world-class event for professional cycling. The placement emerges above all from the direct comparison with three competitions of international importance. Liège-Bastogne-Liège finished in eighth place, La Vuelta a España in ninth and Paris-Roubaix in eleventh. In the portal's ranking, therefore, the Lombard competition precedes all three: an order that brings the Varese race ahead of races indicated as monuments of the discipline. The data concerns the historic race in the Varese area, presented by the source as a world-class event for professional cycling. Seventh place is accompanied by a precise score, 913 points, and by an equally precise comparison with the tests that follow in the list. The ranking thus compares the Tre Valli with the international events mentioned by the portal. For the Lombardy competition, the heart of the news is the combination of placement and score. The race is seventh, while the three races mentioned are behind: Liège-Bastogne-Liège eighth, La Vuelta a España ninth and Paris-Roubaix eleventh. The comparison assigns the Tre Valli a higher position than those three competitions in the ProCyclingStats ranking. The recognition, therefore, has a precise form: a seventh place obtained with 913 points, ahead of Liège-Bastogne-Liège, the Vuelta and Paris-Roubaix. The source presents this order as confirmation of the world level of the historic Varese race in professional cycling. ### The internal metric of the portal The ranking drawn up by ProCyclingStats does not coincide with the official ranking of the International Cycling Union (UCI). To build the ranking, the portal applies an autonomous criterion that measures the overall strength of the runners at the start. The result of a competition therefore depends on the sum of the individual odds of the cyclists lined up at the start. The calculation starts from the ranking of the individual athletes. The presence of a cyclist in the top ten in the world ranking is worth 50 points for the race. For subsequent positions, the score decreases progressively up to a point for athletes placed within the first thousand places. The sum of these odds produces the score assigned to the race and allows PCs to sort competitions based on the level of the group of starters. It is this approach that gives technical meaning to the 913 points of the Tre Valli, without transforming them into a figure in the UCI ranking. The statistic measures the value of cyclists present at the start according to the scale of the portal; it is not presented by the source as the official ranking of international cycling. At the top of the list, ahead of the Lombard competition, is the Tour de France, which leads with 1567 points. The top positions also include the World Road Championships, Lombardy, Milan-Sanremo, the Giro d 'Italia and the Tirreno-Adriatico. The list indicates the small group of tests that precedes the Tre Valli in the ProCyclingStats ranking and completes the numerical table of the ranking. The score is then linked to the sum of the individual odds and the ranking band occupied by each athlete at the start. The internal metric of the portal translates the value of the group of starters into numbers according to the scale described by the source. The calendar and the local reaction The calendar of the Tre Valli Varesine decisively influences the success of the race. Its proximity to Il Lombardia leads top teams to field their captains in Varese. Participation allows them to refine their preparation and check their condition ahead of the Classic of the Dead Leaves. For the Varese race, therefore, the calendar position is linked to the possibility of having the captains of the top teams at the start. The source presents this proximity to Il Lombardia as an element that supports the success of the competition and leads the top teams to use Varese to fine-tune preparation and verify physical condition. The data also confirm the ongoing growth path of the competition. Two years after its last appearance in the Top 10, the Tre Valli Varesine has returned to the group of the world’s top ten races. The ranking figure is thus accompanied by a recent precedent of the same race, cited to describe its growth. The reference to the assessor’s words is the coincidence with the continental exhibition held in Ljubljana, Slovenia. After commenting on the European championship, Malerba added a clarification aimed at those who had raised objections about the presence of potholes along the route, considered dangerous for the athletes. The source therefore records, alongside the sporting recognition, also the local debate on the route and the calendar choice. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/tre-valli-varesine-al-7-posto-mondiale-per-livello-degli-atleti-supera-parigi-roubaix-e-vuelta/2710684/)*

item.title: Construction sites in Lugano: the City Council aims to reduce inconvenience
item.description: The Municipality answers Michele Codella's question Work in Lugano will also continue in the coming years Focus between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Municipality answers Michele Codella's question - Work in Lugano will continue in the coming years - Focus between Botta Shelter and Corso Pestalozzi - The interventions in Molino Nuovo are close to completion ## Key facts - Question → Michele Codella - Construction works in progress → Besso and Genzana underpass - Project → StazLu - Future area → Botta shelter – Corso Pestalozzi - Road works → via Madonnetta, via la Santa and via Pazzalino - Subjects cited → AIL and Canton - Expected effect → contain time, costs and inconvenience - Recipients → citizens, users and economic activities In Lugano, the Municipality responded to Michele Codella's question on construction sites that complicate the lives of citizens. The Executive has outlined the coordination of the work of the coming years and the ways to mitigate its impact on the population. In recent years, Lugano has been affected by significant infrastructure works, which will continue in the future. The Municipality is therefore called upon to allow large construction sites to coexist with the interventions that the City cannot renounce, including road and infrastructural maintenance works connected to the credits intended for the extraordinary maintenance of the city roads and the canal network. ### The areas indicated by the Municipality The StazLu project includes the construction sites underway in Besso and the Genzana underpass. In the coming years, the focus of the interventions will be the area between the Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi, where the Piazzale ex Scuole will be redeveloped, the tram-train network will be built and the underground infrastructure will be renewed. Faced with the concentration of interventions, the Municipality aims to make the various clients collaborate. The intent is to avoid, as far as possible, that the construction sites follow each other separately, coordinate the different operational phases and limit the overall impact on citizens, users and economic activities. According to the Executive, this method should help reduce time, costs and inconvenience. Extraordinary maintenance is also part of the planning: in the most demanding phases of large construction sites, the City intends to place work on roads and pipelines outside the Centre. It is with this in mind that the works were organized between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the roundabout of via Ruvigliana, along via Madonnetta, via la Santa and via Pazzalino. Now close to completion, they include the renewal of the underground infrastructure, carried out by the AIL, and the laying of the sound-absorbing asphalt, managed by the Canton. For those who reach Lugano for work, including cross-border commuters, the Municipality's response does not provide a timetable or an alternative route. The practical fact that emerges is another: the management of the works should focus on the sequence, so as to avoid maintenance arriving immediately after a large construction site or multiple interventions overlapping in the Centre. It doesn't mean jobs are cancelled. The strategy described by the City tries to bring together different works: on the one hand the tram-train, the redevelopment of the former School Square and the underground infrastructures in the central area; on the other, the maintenance of the roads and the drainage network. For users, the expected benefit is not the absence of construction sites, but a reduction in overall impact, time and inconvenience. ### Before and after: the stated logic | Situation to avoid | Choice indicated by the Municipality | |---|---| | Succession of separate construction sites | Coordination between different clients | | Maintenance superimposed on the most demanding phases in the Center | Programming outside the Center | | Molino Nuovo works contemporary with the large central construction sites | Advancement of interventions to limit the repercussions on traffic | For a cross-border worker, this distinction helps to read the news without turning it into a calendar that the source does not provide. Besso and the Genzana underpass belong to the works already in progress; the area between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi is indicated as the main fire in the coming years; the interventions between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the via Ruvigliana roundabout are instead described as close to completion. These are three different situations and do not authorize us to deduce times, closures or diversions. The answer puts citizens, users and economic activities on the same level. For this reason, planning does not only concern circulation, but also the impact on economic activities. The Municipality does not promise that every inconvenience will be eliminated: it indicates the objective of reducing it while the necessary works are carried out. To transform the answer into a useful reading grid for those who work in Lugano, the cross-border worker can follow a simple sequence, without attributing information to the source that it does not contain. ### Four operational steps 1. Identify the area. Distinguish between Besso and the Genzana underpass, where works are already underway as part of StazLu; the area between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi, indicated for the next few years; and the stretch between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the Via Ruvigliana roundabout, where the works are close to completion. 2. Associate the intervention. For the central area, the municipal response refers to the Piazzale ex Scuole, the tram-train network and the renewal of the underground infrastructure. In Molino Nuovo, however, it indicates the renewal of the underground infrastructure entrusted to the AIL and the laying of the sound-absorbing asphalt by the Canton. 3. Read the sequence. The City will try to schedule extraordinary maintenance of roads and pipelines outside the Center during the most demanding phases of large construction sites. The works at Molino Nuovo were brought forward compared to the start of the large construction sites in the Center precisely to avoid overlaps. 4. Separate goal and result. Reducing inconvenience is the objective declared by the Municipality. However, the response does not quantify the effect on circulation and does not set a detailed timetable. This procedure does not produce an itinerary, travel time, or detour. It helps you understand which phase your move concerns and so as not to confuse construction sites already underway, works planned in the coming years and interventions nearing completion. For those who travel through Lugano for work, including cross-border commuters, it is a more solid distinction than any route obtained by deduction. If the reference is Molino Nuovo, the point to follow is the anticipation of the works compared to the Center. If the reference is the central area, the data to follow is the coordination between clients. If the reference is Besso or the Genzana underpass, the answer instead places them among the interventions already underway. In all cases, the Municipality links planning to the need to guarantee the works and reduce the impact on citizens, users and economic activities. To combine this local reading with a work travel monitoring tool, consult the storico traffico e code ai valichi. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/politica/1957269/cantieri-interventi-lavori-evitare-anni-esecutivo-municipio-disagi-obiettivo-vita)*

item.title: Cc-Ti Assembly: the economy is not the State's ATM
item.description: The Cc-Ti meets today in Bellinzona Gehri calls for healthy finances and a vision of the country Albertoni supports a stop to the increase in cantonal employees
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Cc-Ti meets today in Bellinzona - Gehri calls for healthy finances and a vision of the country - Albertoni supports the stop to the increase in cantonal employees - Albertoni rules out heavy cuts to services
## Key facts - Event: 109th assembly of the Cc-Ti - Location: Bellinzona - President: Andrea Gehri - Priorities: healthy finances, economy free to grow, trained young people and vision of the country - Initiative: Stop the increase in cantonal employees
At the 109th assembly of the Chamber of Commerce of the Canton of Ticino, held today in Bellinzona, the message was clear: Ticino must find its compass again and the economy cannot be called upon to pay the bill. Andrea Gehri, president of Cc-Ti, has indicated four priorities: restoring finances, encouraging economic growth, training young people ready for future challenges and promoting a vision of a country capable of uniting everyone, from right to left.
### Criticism of politics
Gehri did not name names, but criticized the political management. In his opinion, politics addresses the ordinary without governing the extraordinary.
> «Politics is managing the ordinary, but not the extraordinary».
In the president's message there is no mea culpa aimed at businesses. Companies, according to Gehri, work very quietly, they do not ask for subsidies and instead ask for framework conditions that allow them to prosper. The contested point is the withdrawal from the economy for decisions which, in its reading, do not fall within the economic competence.
The examples cited include the thirteenth AVS initiative and two initiatives relating to health insurance premiums. Gehri observed that in these cases money is spent without knowing where to get it first. It did not close the door to an intervention on revenues, if included in the symmetry of sacrifices. The proposal is to sit at the same table with politics, social partners and civil society: the Cc-Ti, he said, is available.
### Administration at the center
Director Luca Albertoni has broadened the picture. Doing business is more difficult not only in Ticino, but also in the context of the German crisis and American tariffs. Hence Cc-Ti's support for the Stop the increase in cantonal employees initiative, with the Chamber on the promoting committee.
Albertoni assured that heavy cuts to services are not needed. He calls for bringing the administration back to normal proportions, so that the state is effective for the citizens. Some tasks, he added, could pass to the private sector. But he said he doesn't believe there will be a bloodbath in the end: that's not the aim of the initiative. For those who live across the border and work in the Canton of Ticino, the connection with the assembly is real but indirect. The news talks about political directions, framework conditions for businesses and the size of the administration; does not communicate an immediate change to a paycheck, leave or benefit.
### The boundary between message and measurement
A cross-border worker can therefore read the text as a signal on the way in which the Cc-Ti would like to direct the debate, not as a new rule to be applied. The reference to the thirteenth AVS and to the initiatives on health insurance premiums remains a criticism of the procurement of resources. The source does not indicate amounts, deadlines, rates, documents or procedures.
The same applies to the initiative on cantonal employees. Albertoni speaks of an administration that needs to be brought back to normal proportions and admits that some tasks could pass to the private sector. However, it does not indicate which tasks, which services or which positions would be involved. He adds that he does not believe in a final bloodbath and specifies that that is not the aim. For a worker, therefore, the text does not allow anticipating a transfer, a reduction or a new hire.
For the cross-border worker, the second plan concerns personal issues that are not regulated here: G permit, AVS, LPP, KVG, refunds and withholding tax. The presence of the word AVS in the speech does not transform the meeting into a social security announcement; similarly, the reference to health insurance premiums does not define a KVG procedure. This distinction avoids confusing the debate on public spending with the rules of professional life across borders.
| Theme | Reported data | What doesn't appear | | Economy | Businesses demand framework conditions | An application measure is not indicated | | Administration | Some tasks may go private | No tasks or times are indicated | | Employment | Albertoni does not believe in a final bloodbath | There is no outcome indicated on the seats |
The prudent reading is this: the Cc-Ti asks for political direction, but the source does not yet describe a concrete change for the cross-border worker. To transform the message of the assembly into a useful reading, the cross-border worker can follow a simple sequence and not confuse the positions with the effects already in force.
### Four steps
1. Attribute each proposal. The general priorities and the call to the table with politics, social partners and civil society belong to Andrea Gehri's speech. The support for Stop the increase in cantonal employees and the evaluation of the tasks for the private sector are instead presented by Luca Albertoni.
2. Separate the proposal from the decision. The source reports Cc-Ti's support for the initiative, but does not report an outcome, an application date or a list of offices involved. Until these elements appear, the initiative cannot be read as a change that is already operational.
3. Isolate your personal theme. If the application concerns permit G, AVS, LPP, KVG, refunds or withholding tax, this meeting does not provide a new amount, a new deadline or a new procedure in the text reported. The reference to the thirteenth AVS and health insurance premiums should be left within the scope of the debate on public resources.
4. Look for the concrete fact. To understand if a political position really affects work in Ticino, it is necessary to wait for the possible indication of a service, of a task transferred to the private sector or of a decision on the framework conditions. The source does not attribute specific consequences to individual workers or categories.
### What remains today
The news therefore offers a reading grid, not a practice to present. The cross-border worker can distinguish the discussion on the economic direction of the Canton of Ticino from the rules of his own situation. There are no deadlines to meet or documents to deliver from the source.
The practical value of the distinction is to avoid attributing to Cc-Ti a decision that the source does not report. The positions are defined; the next step, however, is not described in the available text.
To measure an already defined tax situation, you can use the calcolatore fiscale.
*Source: [ticinonews.ch](https://www.ticinonews.ch/ticino/gehri-leconomia-non-e-il-bancomat-dello-stato-444773)*

item.title: PATTI CHIARI Cadenazzo, traffic lights come on… and protests flare up
item.description: 73% opposed to the project voted on May 19, 2019 First traffic lights in Cadenazzo on August 29 last year USTRA estimates a 30% saving in 2028 Vote → 73% of votes
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 73% opposed to the project voted on May 19, 2019 - First traffic lights in Cadenazzo on August 29 last - USTRA estimates a 30% saving in 2028
## Key facts - Vote → 73% of votes against - Route → Cadenazzo-Quartino, Piano di Magadino - Project → FEDRO - Overall cost → approximately 40 million francs - Deadline indicated → end 2027 for the progressive replacement - Estimate → approximately 30% at peak times in 2028
On 19 May 2019, the population of Ticino rejected, with 73% of votes against, a cantonal project which provided for traffic lights along the route between Cadenazzo and Quartino, instead of roundabouts. Seven years later, on August 29th, the first systems were installed in Cadenazzo.
The program concerns the Magadino Plan. Further installations are planned: by the end of 2027, the roundabouts between Cadenazzo and Quartino will be gradually replaced by traffic lights. The initiative was born from a study and a decision by FEDRO, the Federal Roads Office. In 2020, the road became federal property; until then it was cantonal.
### Investment and objectives
The total expected expenditure amounts to approximately 40 million francs: eight million will be allocated to traffic lights and the remaining 32 million to the improvement of the entire road network. For the FEDRO, the objectives are to make traffic more fluid and increase safety on a road traveled by almost 30,000 vehicles a day, which has always been among the busiest in the Canton of Ticino.
The first phase, however, produced negative reactions. In September, in the weeks following the installation in Cadenazzo, numerous motorists reported queues and longer journey times. In some cases, they reported, the times doubled or tripled.
The traffic lights located in front of the Cadenazzo roundabout, the only one destined not to be eliminated, also remain at the center of the debate, as well as the requirement to turn right leaving via Stradonino, which connects Gudo to Cadenazzo. Patti Chiari's crew documented the complex maneuvers required by buses and trucks, which obstruct the flow of traffic.
The protests led Claudio Isabella, grand councilor of the Centre, and seven other parliamentarians from different parties to question the cantonal government. Simone Gianini, liberal national councilor, instead asked Bern for explanations. The Federal Council responded that it is premature to draw conclusions and that the effectiveness will be assessed after the conclusion of the work. ## What to measure before judging
For a cross-border commuter traveling the Cadenazzo-Quartino route, the practical question is whether the time lost in the first weeks represents the outcome of the project or a settling-in phase. The source describes both situations, but at different times. Confusing the September protest with the forecast for 2028 would make the picture simpler than it is.
### Four moments, four interpretations
| Moment | Reported data | Cautious interpretation | |---|---|---| | First days | Accidents, sensor malfunctions that were later corrected, and optimization work | Problematic phase | | September | Queues and travel times reported as doubled or tripled in some cases | Disruption reported by motorists | | Early October | Travel times practically the same as those in the same period the previous year, according to USTRA | Stabilized situation | | 2028 | Estimated savings of about 30% during peak hours | Expected result once the project is completed |
The transition from one row to the next is the central point for those who use the road to get to work. USTRA acknowledged that the first days in the Cadenazzo area were problematic, but also reported that by early October the situation had already stabilized. The comparison with the same period the previous year does not erase the queues reported in September; it does, however, show that the initial figure is not presented as definitive.
For a cross-border commuter, the 30% estimate therefore does not represent time already saved. It is a forecast linked to the completion of the intervention and peak hours. Likewise, reports of doubling and tripling do not automatically describe the final outcome: the source places them in the weeks following the initial installation.
The cause of the disruption is also described in a nuanced way. Italo Broggini, head of the USTRA project, cited accidents, malfunctions of the new sensors, and optimization work. The presence of multiple factors makes it unwise to judge the entire project based on a single incident.
The response of the Federal Council points in the same direction: it is still too early to assess the actual effectiveness of the entire project. For those crossing the Magadino Plain, the distinction between observed data, a stabilized phase, and a future estimate offers a concrete way to interpret any delays without turning a forecast into a guarantee. ## How to follow the transition phase
Those who cross the Magadino Plain for work can read the timeline operationally, without anticipating the final outcome. The soundest procedure is to separate the section travelled, the date of the experience and the data used for comparison.
### Four steps
1. Identify the route segment. Check whether your route includes Cadenazzo-Quartino, the Cadenazzo area or the via Stradonino exit, connecting Gudo and Cadenazzo. These are the points mentioned in Patti chiari's reconstruction.
2. Place the episode on the timeline. On August 29 last year, the first traffic lights were installed in Cadenazzo; in September, reports of queues and longer travel times emerged; at the beginning of October, USTRA reported stabilization. Separating these phases avoids improper comparisons.
3. Compare the time with the benchmark used by USTRA. The comparison published by the Federal Roads Office concerns the travel time for the route during the same period of the previous year. The forecast of around 30% instead concerns peak hours in 2028, when the project will be completed.
4. Keep the expected result distinct from the verified result. The replacement of the roundabouts will continue progressively through the end of 2027. Only after the works are completed, according to the Federal Council's response, will it be possible to assess the actual effectiveness of the project as a whole.
For those travelling by car, the observation must also include the configuration indicated in front of the Cadenazzo roundabout, the only one that will not be dismantled. If the route involves via Stradonino, the obligation to turn right must be taken into account; the program documented that buses and trucks may be forced into laborious maneuvers. However, this data does not justify automatically extending that pattern to every vehicle or every day.
This framework enables the cross-border commuter to read the project in phases: concrete experience, stabilization communicated by USTRA and final forecast. There is no need to choose today between promise and protest; one needs to know which data is being observed and what deadline it refers to. The 30% estimate remains tied to 2028, while assessments of effectiveness await the end of the works.
To compare waiting times at the crossings used on the cross-border journey, consult storico traffico/code ai valichi.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/la1/programmi/informazione/patti-chiari/Cadenazzo-si-accendono-semafori%E2%80%A6-e-proteste--4160668.html)*

item.title: Industry in Ticino: staff shortages and innovation
item.description: In the last 18 months, numerous layoffs in Ticino’s industry Fifteen collective redundancies recorded over the past year and a half Approximately 16 thousand
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Numerous layoffs in Ticino’s industry over the last 18 months - Fifteen collective layoffs recorded over the last year and a half - Around 16 thousand cross-border workers work in industry - More than half are over fifty
## Key facts - Period → last eighteen months - Collective dismissals followed → fifteen in the last year and a half - Order portfolio → satisfactory for the coming months - Cross-border workers in industry → approximately 16 thousand - Female and cross-border workers lost → around 900 in two years - Age → more than half are over fifty - Survey cited → 2022 - Interviewees → Stefano Modenini and Daniele Duma
In the last eighteen months, in Ticino, collective layoffs in the industrial sector have been numerous and have fueled concern for the future of the sector. The question posed by the source is therefore precise: does the problem arise from the economic situation or from the choices that guide companies in subsequent years?
Stefano Modenini, director of the Ticino Industries Association, believes that the current phase is less worrying than it appeared at the beginning of the year. The majority of companies consider their order book to be satisfactory for the months to come. Stability, however, does not equate to a guarantee of continuity. In the last year and a half Modenini has followed fifteen collective dismissals: half in the industrial world, the others in the tertiary sector.
### From the economic situation to corporate choices
A collective dismissal, according to the director of AITI, does not necessarily derive from an economic crisis. A company can decide to diversify production or to favor other production locations. The attractiveness of the territory compared to other regions also plays a role in this choice: legal stability, taxation, costs and availability of manpower are conditions that can reduce the risk of a transfer.
The pressure does not only come from US tariffs, the automotive crisis, the strong franc or the cost of energy. The source also mentions the increase in transport costs due to wars and the interruption of some communication routes. Modenini notes, however, that the duties affected a very limited part of Swiss companies.
On the development front, the challenge indicated is innovation. Bringing innovation into companies involves allocating resources to tools, training and reviewing processes. The technical quality and ability to innovate of Swiss industry are recognized globally; for this reason, according to the source, Switzerland should invest more in professional training. The Innovation Law offers financing tools, while more targeted support is needed for small and medium-sized enterprises. Finally, research already benefits from collaboration with academic partners such as SUPSI.
The source combines the point of view of the employers with that of the workers: in addition to Modenini, Daniele Duma, head of the fusion department of the GF of Novazzano, was interviewed. The future of the Ticino industry is thus read through two perspectives, management and work. ## Why the issue concerns those who work across the border
For a cross-border worker, the most concrete part of the interview concerns the availability of qualified personnel. Modenini links the shortage not only to the demographic crisis, but also to the new tax agreement with neighboring Italy on the taxation of cross-border workers, identified as an aggravating factor, especially in Ticino. The source does not, however, describe the agreement’s individual effects on personal matters: the data presented concerns the labor market.
According to the statistics cited in the interview, in two years Canton Ticino lost around 900 female and male cross-border workers, partly for age-related reasons. In the industrial sector, there are around 16 thousand cross-border workers, and more than half are over fifty. For high-value-added companies, Modenini says, the availability of trained and qualified people is the main problem; without labor, some activities could disappear.
### What changes in day-to-day work
The practical reading does not lead to a single answer. Automation is identified as one way to address the shortage, but the source pairs this measure with greater participation by women and young people in the labor market. The issue is organizational: many young people want part-time employment, while work-family balance is identified as a priority. Some company collective agreements already provide for Fridays off, a sign of the demands that are becoming increasingly important for workers.
| Pressure identified | Response mentioned in the source | |---|---| | Staff shortage | Automation and greater participation in work | | Demand for work-family balance | Part-time work and, in some agreements, Fridays off | | Lack of technical profiles | Vocational training and courses for companies |
For those who work across the border, the implication is concrete but limited: the future of a job also depends on skills, work-schedule organization and the company’s ability to adopt new technologies. However, no personal calculation or tax procedure can be derived from the interview. G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax, INPS and double taxation remain outside the scope of the text. The only explicit cross-border link is the effect of the tax agreement on the availability of labor in Ticino. ## How to read the situation and find one's bearings
Anyone wishing to assess an opportunity in Ticino's industry can use four steps drawn from the source. It is not a tax procedure or a salary calculation: it serves to assess the company, skills and development.
### 1. Clarify the company's direction
The first is to distinguish the short term from the development plan. A company may have satisfactory orders for the coming months and, at the same time, direct production toward another site or a different activity. Faced with a reorganization, the question is what strategic direction supports it, without taking for granted that collective redundancy coincides with an economic crisis.
### 2. Compare the profile with demand
The second starts from the 2022 survey cited by Modenini. The profiles most needed are intermediate-level ones with partly technical vocational training, from production operators to automation operators. The information offers a criterion for assessing a role or a training path: check the importance of technical skills. AITI offers courses to companies; the source also reports a shortage of apprentices in the more technological industry compared with the tertiary sector.
### 3. Look for the substance of innovation
The third is to distinguish words from processes. Innovation requires tools, training and process updates. The picture is heterogeneous: some companies have yet to take the first step toward digitalization, while others are incorporating artificial intelligence. It is therefore advisable to observe which investments and skills are associated with the role, without turning artificial intelligence into an automatic explanation for every change.
### 4. Separate funding and research
The last concerns support for development. The Innovation Law provides funding tools, but Modenini believes more targeted measures are necessary for small and medium-sized enterprises. Collaboration with academic partners such as SUPSI, on the other hand, is described as positive: these are two distinct areas, funding and research.
The text does not provide amounts, deadlines or documents for cross-border commuters. It offers a framework for assessing companies, roles and training in the Canton of Ticino. To look for opportunities consistent with the profiles described, consult annunci di lavoro

item.title: Lugano: new allowance for internships in 2027
item.description: One-off allowance: 2,000 francs gross for 12 months Budget 2027: 700,000 to 755,000 francs Estimated lower cost: 30,700 francs 43% of the budget.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - One-off allowance: 2,000 francs gross for 12 months' pay - Budget 2027: 700,000 to 755,000 francs - Estimated lower cost: 30,700 francs - 43% of the budget is allocated to internships
## Key facts - City → Lugano - New allowance → 2,000 gross francs per month for 12 months - Budget 2027 → 755,000 francs - Progression passed → 2'600, 3'120 and 3'640 francs - Internship fee → 43% of the budget
In the 2027 Budget, the Municipality of Lugano increased the budget allocated to training staff by 55,000 francs: from 700,000 to 755,000 francs. The choice accompanies the confirmation of the reduction in compensation for professional internships in the City.
The new approach provides for a single allowance of 2,000 gross francs per month for 12 months. The previous progression is thus abandoned, which provided for 2,600, 3,120 and 3,640 francs for 12 months. The Municipality explains that that system was introduced when internships could last even several years and recognized economic progression over time.
The Municipality illustrated the revision by responding to the question of the municipal councilor Edoardo Cappelletti (Pc), which began as an interpellation. The Executive specifies that the change was not promoted to achieve savings on staff in training. Any reduction in spending, in its reconstruction, is a financial effect of the change and not its purpose.
### The motivation of the Municipality
According to the City, the new scheme takes into account changes in training methods, in the needs of study paths, in the reference management framework and in the job market. For the Executive, internships now play an important role in training, professionally orienting and bringing young people closer to the public sector.
Hence the choice to harmonize the treatment of people in training and to adopt allowances considered balanced and adequate for the purposes of the individual courses. The Municipality wants to overcome differences that it believes are no longer fully justified by the current context.
The response also reports a significant reduction in both the number and duration of professional internships promoted by the municipal administration. The document indicates the introduction of the Minimum Wage Law and the related regulation as the prevailing cause; the regulatory framework allows internships to be promoted only when specific conditions are respected.
The financial data should be read in conjunction with the expansion of the types of internships offered. 43% of the 755,000 francs of the budget for staff in training is allocated to staff on internships. For this reason, the Municipality disputes the assertion that the City saves money on young people in training and on interns. For those who live on the border and are considering a training or work course in Ticino, the concrete significance of the news must be limited to the remuneration of internships in the City of Lugano. The examined answer does not indicate residency or application requirements and does not deal with G permit, AVS, LPP, KVG, refunds, withholding tax or double taxation. The connection with the border crosser therefore remains limited to the interest in an internship in the City of Lugano: from the source it cannot be deduced who can access the routes.
### How to read numbers
The first comparison to make separates the individual compensation from the overall cost. The 30,700 francs are not presented as an equal reduction for each intern. The Municipality calculated that lower cost by applying the new rates to the volume of administrative students and professional internships last year. The figure therefore describes a hypothesis referring to the volume of activity of the previous year.
The second comparison concerns the budget. In the same passage in which it indicates the lower cost, the Municipality communicates that the budget for training staff rises from 700,000 to 755,000 francs in the transition from the 2026 Budget to the 2027 Budget. 43% is allocated to internships and the types offered are expanded. The two data do not describe the same quantity: the first concerns the application of the new rates to a past number of routes; the second concerns the overall allocation foreseen for personnel in training.
The third element is the structure of the offer. The source says that the number and duration of internships have been reduced, especially as a result of the Minimum Wage Law and related regulations, but he also says that the types have been broadened. For anyone reading a proposal, this means that knowing the monthly allowance is not enough to reconstruct the duration or nature of the route. The text does not list the types and does not specify the precise conditions applicable to individual internships.
Comparison with other references must also be kept within its limits. The Municipality considers the "Practitioner's Charter", prepared by the Bar Association of the Canton of Ticino, to be a set of recommendations with no binding value. The City considers the 2,000 gross monthly francs adequate: the amount is aligned with the cantonal administration internships and compatible with the other tertiary level internship paths contemplated by the new structure. However, the source does not provide a net calculation or a comparison between professions. Whoever needs to use this information to evaluate an internship can proceed without transforming the municipal data into a general rule. The source does not publish an application process or a list of available positions - it offers checks to apply to the proposal.
### Five checks before comparison
1. Identify the route. The answer distinguishes administrative students from professional internships. Before comparing the amounts, you need to understand which of the two categories the position described belongs to.
2. Check the compensation structure. The reference indicated by the Municipality is a single allowance of 2,000 gross monthly francs for 12 months. Gross and duration of payments must be read together; the source does not allow that data to be transformed into a net amount.
3. Separate the current model from the previous one. The progression of 2'600, 3'120 and 3'640 francs for 12 months belongs to the abandoned system. Its reference serves historical comparison, it does not authorize us to consider it still in force.
4. Don't confuse budget with compensation. The 30,700 francs are the lowest cost calculated by applying the new rates to the number of journeys last year. They are not the amount to be deducted from a single person's allowance. The 2027 budget of 755,000 francs instead concerns all staff in training, with 43% allocated to internships.
5. Check the path frame. The Municipality reports that the Law on the minimum wage and the related regulation allow internships only under specific conditions. The source does not list them: it is not possible to reconstruct documents, deadlines or administrative steps not indicated. The typologies have been expanded, but the list is not provided.
For a cross-border worker, this grid avoids attributing answers to the allowance alone that the article does not contain. The text does not clarify what the treatment of an applicant would be with regards to the G permit, AVS, BVG, KVG, refunds, withholding tax or double taxation. These are issues external to the Municipality's response and cannot be obtained from the 2,000 gross francs.
The reference used by the City remains verifiable: the amount is considered adequate, the Practitioner's Charter of the Bar Association of the Canton of Ticino has the value of a recommendation and the amount is indicated as consistent with the internships of the cantonal administration and with the other tertiary level courses of the new approach. Those looking for an opportunity can start from the distinction between type, duration and compensation, without adding conditions not described by the source.
To explore professional opportunities in Ticino, consult the annunci di lavoro.

item.description: More than 50% shift to the Suzhou site 40% impact on the production area 30% impact on the white-collar area Strike, garrison and agitation
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - More than 50% shift to the Suzhou site - 40% impact on the production floor - 30% impact on white-collar area - Strike, garrison and agitation to the bitter end
## Key facts - Company → Barco di Saronno - Destination → Suzhou site, China - Production to China → over 50% - Production area impact → 40% - Impact on the white collar area → 30% - Failure to renew contracts → 25 workers - Mobilization → strike with garrison and demonstration in the square - State → endless agitation
### Management's announcement
Today in Saronno the mobilization of Barco workers took shape with a demonstration and a demonstration in the square. The protest follows management's announcement that more than 50% of production will be relocated to the Suzhou, China site.
The announcement also includes a corporate reorganization. The source indicates two distinct impacts: 40% on the production area and 30% on the white collar area. The percentages therefore concern two different internal areas, mentioned separately in the communication: on the one hand the production area, on the other the clerical area.
The framework presented to workers combines a decision on the location of production and a change in company organization. The first concerns the transfer to Suzhou of more than half of the production; the second is described through the percentages referring to the two areas. These are the elements indicated by the Management and recalled in the news of the day in Saronno.
The response was organized in the same place where the demonstration took place. Unions, RSU and workers proclaimed a strike, accompanied by a demonstration and a demonstration in the square. Added to today's mobilization is the declaration of an all-out state of agitation, reported together with the other initiatives.
The passage described is clear: the announcement of the move of production to China is followed by a public protest by Barco workers. The reorganization is seen within the same story because it was announced together with the transfer to Suzhou. The production and clerical areas are both recalled, but with different impacts: 40% for the first and 30% for the second.
For Saronno, the visible data is the garrison with demonstration in the square; for Barco, the industrial data is the shift of over 50% of production to the Chinese site. The source places the management's decision and the immediate reaction of unions, RSU and workers on the same level, without separating the production transfer from the announced reorganization. ### The consequences indicated by the unions
The second element of the story concerns a consequence which, according to the unions, has already occurred. Fim Territorio Laghi, Fiom Varese, Uilm Varese and Rsu link the announcement to the non-renewal of contracts for 25 workers. The data is presented by the acronyms as a consequence already produced by the announced choice.
The reference to the 25 workers adds to the discussion on the percentages an outcome already indicated in the source. The reorganization and move announced by the Management are recalled by the unions together with that non-renewal. Their reading moves on two levels: on the one hand the industrial announcement, on the other the contractual impact which, according to their explanation, has already emerged.
> «Workers are neither numbers nor percentages».
With this sentence the acronyms reiterate the center of their protest. The call to workers comes after the indication of 40% for the production area, 30% for the white-collar area and the shift of over 50% of production to Suzhou. The union reaction disputes that the matter is considered only through values ​​and quotas, bringing attention back to the people involved, as declared by the representatives themselves.
The same acronyms define the non-renewal as a further mockery. The term accompanies the passage in which the unions point out that the non-renewal has already affected 25 workers. The protest therefore does not arise only from the description of the reorganization: for the representations, the announcement is also linked to the contractual consequence already indicated.
The role of Fim Territorio Laghi, Fiom Varese, Uilm Varese and Rsu emerges in the explanation of the consequences and in taking a position on workers. The phrase on people, together with the reference to non-renewal, defines the tone of the reaction: the percentages communicated by the Management are accompanied by data on workers, that of the 25 contracts not renewed. ### All-out mobilization
The sequel indicated by the source is the state of endless agitation. The mobilization is not described only through today's initiative in Saronno: unions, RSU and workers have declared a strike with a demonstration and demonstration in the square, adding to these initiatives the state of unrest. The formula is reported as part of the response that arrived immediately after the Management's announcement.
The strike constitutes the form of protest indicated for the day, while the demonstration and the demonstration make the presence of the workers in the square visible. The source presents the three actions in the same passage and attributes the decision to unions, RSU and workers. The sequel to the story therefore remains linked to the mobilization declared in Saronno and its continuation to the bitter end.
The news links the present of the protest to the choice not to stop the response with today's protest alone. The state of all-out agitation is in fact indicated together with the strike and the demonstration, as part of the reaction of the workers and their representatives. The square is the location of the initiative described today; endless agitation is the dimension that accompanies her beyond the day.
The text underlines that the answer came immediately. After the announcement, the declaration of the strike, the demonstration, the demonstration and the state of agitation constitute a single front of initiatives. The presence of unions, RSU and workers is indicated as a common element of the decisions taken.
The term indefinitely gives the key to the sequel: the mobilization is not described as having ended with today's demonstration. The matter remains open on the protest level, with the state of unrest declared alongside the strike and the demonstration. For Saronno, the documented sequel is therefore that of the mobilization already declared. The state of endless agitation remains the passage that the source indicates for the phase following the demonstration.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/ne-numeri-ne-percentuali-la-rabbia-dei-lavoratori-barco-di-saronno-dopo-lannuncio-del-trasferimento-in-cina/2710603/)*
