## Key facts - Gross median wage in Ticino → 5,708 francs per month in 2024 - Swiss average → 7,024 francs per month in 2024 - Statistical source → Federal Statistical Office - Survey → latest SUPSI survey - One year after graduation → 93% of the graduates interviewed are working or continuing their studies - Among those who work → 76% are employed in Ticino - Author → Luca Frasa
### The choice after training In 2024, the median gross monthly salary in Ticino stood at 5,708 francs, compared to the Swiss average of 7,024 francs. According to the Federal Statistical Office, the gap, which can also be traced back to the structure of our economy, is significant. For those evaluating professional opportunities, this gap can guide the choice between staying in the Canton and looking elsewhere.
Luca Frasa starts from this situation. After studying, training and obtaining a diploma or degree, a young person may find himself faced with the choice between staying in Ticino and seeking better professional prospects elsewhere. The point does not coincide with simply entering the world of work. The issue also includes the possibility of developing a professional path, achieving a certain economic autonomy and, perhaps, starting a family in one's own Canton.
However, an indicator linked to training introduces a positive note. According to the latest SUPSI survey, one year after obtaining the qualification, 93% of the graduates interviewed were working or continuing their studies. Of those who worked, 76% were employed in Ticino. For Frasa, these percentages indicate that in Ticino there are opportunities and companies capable of making use of skills.
The comparison between the two values, alone, does not exhaust the topic. The reflection also concerns what comes after entering work: a career, a certain economic independence and the possibility of starting a family in one's own Canton. For this reason the source clearly distinguishes employment from professional growth. Having a job and being able to build a path are not the same thing. ### The margin of companies The business picture completes the reflection on the prospects of young people. Not everyone can become a manager, and it is unrealistic to expect every company to guarantee salaries equal to those of the large economic centers beyond the Gotthard. Small and medium-sized businesses in Ticino also have to face costs, competition and the difficulty of finding qualified personnel. The source recalls these limits without denying them and asks to address the topic concretely.
The directions indicated start from the connection between training and the world of work. Alongside this, it is necessary to encourage the arrival of activities with high added value, support those who invest and generate qualified jobs and expand opportunities for professional growth for young people. The reasoning brings together different needs: the path of those who have trained, the ability of companies to invest and the presence of professional opportunities that do not stop at the first job.
The point is not to ask every company to function like a large economic reality beyond the Gotthard. It means building conditions in which training, investments and qualified jobs can fit into the same plan. Small and medium-sized businesses remain faced with costs, competition and the search for qualified personnel; at the same time, the Canton must question itself on the growth opportunities it can offer to young people.
### The valleys and the local estate Particular attention should be paid to the valleys, where opportunities are inevitably more limited. When a young person leaves, the area risks losing a future family, skills and participation in local life. The theme therefore also concerns the collective dimension of the territory: together with a person, presence, knowledge and participation in the community can disappear. The valleys make visible the link between professional opportunities and the local future. In Frasa's reasoning, supporting skilled jobs also means looking at areas where opportunities are more limited. ### Leaving can be a choice An experience outside Canton can be positive. Comparison with other realities, learning new languages and exposure to larger markets can be enriching both professionally and personally. The departure, therefore, is not presented as an outcome to be avoided in any case. The critical issue arises when leaving the Canton is no longer a voluntary decision, but an obligatory step.
The distinction is the balance point of Luca Frasa's reflection. Young people are not asked to stay in Ticino because of their attachment to the territory. The request is to create the conditions for them to choose to do so. Staying must be a choice made possible by opportunities, not a consequence of the obligation to stay. At the same time, getting to know other markets and learning new languages can continue to be a useful experience for personal and professional growth.
### The future to offer The reflection thus moves on the relationship between training investment and the future of the territory. A Canton that invests in the training of the new generations is also called upon to evaluate what opportunities it can guarantee them tomorrow. The question is not only about obtaining a diploma or a degree, but also about the possibility of starting a career, gaining a certain economic autonomy and, perhaps, building a family in one's own canton.

item.title: Border protection: The UDC initiative is counterproductive
item.description: The CIP-S rejects the UDC initiative by 8 votes to 2.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The CIP-S rejects the UDC initiative by 8 votes to 2. - The text calls for systematic checks at the borders. - Switzerland would not grant asylum to more than 5.000 people a year. - For cross-border commuters, entering Switzerland would be more difficult.
## Key facts - Decision → negative opinion from the CIP-S, 8 votes to 2 - Name → “Stop abuses in asylum!” - Entry → systematic checks of all persons - Asylum → maximum 5.000 people per year - Irregular stay → departure within 90 days - Scenario → external border of the Schengen area
### The committee's vote
In Bern, the Political Institutions Committee of the Council of States expressed a negative opinion, by 8 votes to 2, on the UDC initiative for border protection. The proposal calls for more controls at the borders and maximum limits on the granting of asylum.
Formally, the text is called “Stop abuses in asylum!” Its first package of measures concerns entry: systematic checks of all persons, complete monitoring of border crossings and rejection of anyone who does not meet the conditions for entry.
For cross-border commuters, the most immediate part concerns border crossings. The CIP-S believes that, if the initiative were approved at the ballot box, Switzerland would in all likelihood become an external border of the Schengen area. The consequence identified in the parliamentary services' note is economic damage and more difficult entry for cross-border commuters and tourists.
The text also addresses the number of people to whom Switzerland may grant asylum: no more than 5.000 per year. For those staying irregularly in the country, it provides for an obligation to report to the authorities; employment contracts would be null and void, these people would be excluded from social and health insurance and would have to leave the country within 90 days.
According to the committee, however, these measures would not resolve the problems raised by the initiative, especially those relating to imported crime, and would create new ones. The security assessment is clear-cut: police operations across the border would face serious impediments, while access to international information systems would be lost.
On asylum, the CIP-S expects few changes. The number of applicants could decrease slightly, but in practice people could not be removed as the text calls for. Their status would become more precarious; according to the committee, this could encourage crime and hinder professional and social integration.
The CIP-S's assessment thus links borders, the economy, security and asylum: in its reading, the requested control of entries would not have an isolated effect. It would also affect the movement of cross-border commuters and tourists and activities across the border. ## What changes, according to the commission
### Crossing the border
For cross-border workers, the practical point is to separate access from the rest of the proposal. The CIP-S directly links acceptance to difficulties entering for cross-border commuters and tourists; however, it does not provide a timetable, a duration for the checks or a procedure for border crossings. The text therefore allows a qualitative assessment, not a calculation of the time required.
The difference between the scenarios can be read as follows:
| Area | Initiative scenario | Effect indicated by the CIP-S | |---|---|---| | Entry | systematic checks of all people and staffed border crossings | more difficult entry for cross-border commuters and tourists | | Schengen | Switzerland would in all likelihood be an external border if the initiative were accepted | economic damage | | Security | cross-border police activities obstructed | access to international information systems would be lost | | Asylum | maximum 5.000 people a year | few changes according to the CIP-S |
In the first area, the cross-border commuter is affected as a person entering: the request concerns all people crossing the border. The source offers no basis for distinguishing the impact according to the border crossing or for translating the prediction into a number of minutes. The concrete fact remains the one indicated by the commission: entry would be more difficult.
The second area is security. The obstruction of cross-border police activities is not presented as an effect on wages or contracts, but as a deterioration of the security situation. For those who work across the border, the issue therefore concerns not only crossing: the commission also links the proposal to police activities and access to international information systems.
The third area is asylum. The CIP-S believes that the maximum limit would produce few changes and that newly arrived people could not be removed as requested. This assessment instead points to greater precariousness of status, with possible obstacles to professional and social integration.
The impact on cross-border commuters is therefore concrete when it comes to crossing, but the source does not make it possible to quantify delays, costs or checks. Adding figures or specific procedures would mean going beyond the assessment expressed by the commission. ## How to monitor the situation
### Five steps
For those who work across the border, this is the most reliable reading sequence. It is not an administrative procedure: it serves to avoid confusing the commission's opinion with the possible application of the measures.
1. **Start with the vote.** CIP-S issued an unfavorable opinion with 8 votes against 2. This is the information that describes the commission's position.
2. Check the condition. The effects on crossings are described in the scenario in which the initiative is approved at the ballot box. It is in this case that the possibility of an external border of the Schengen area and more difficult entry arises.
3. Isolate the rules on entry. The text calls for the systematic checking of all people, full coverage of border crossings and the rejection of anyone who does not meet the conditions for entry.
4. Separate asylum and irregular residence. The limit of 5,000 people concerns the granting of asylum. The obligation to notify, the invalidity of employment contracts, exclusion from insurance and departure within 90 days instead refer to those staying irregularly in the country.
5. Check the security aspect. CIP-S's assessment concerns cross-border police activities and access to international information systems.
The only explicit deadline in the text is the 90-day period for leaving the country in the event of irregular residence. The source does not, however, indicate a date for any change to the controls, an entry-into-force schedule or waiting times at border crossings. Sticking to what is written avoids attributing to the proposal numbers it does not provide.
To follow the practical side of the transition without turning the opinion into an estimate, consult tempi di attesa ai valichi.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/politica/1957311/iniziativa-svizzera-udc-frontiere-protezione)*

item.title: Gaggiolo safety speed bump for pedestrians and workers
item.description: The new speed bump has been installed at the Gaggiolo border crossing.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The new speed bump has been installed at the Gaggiolo border crossing. - The UDSC links it to safety, especially at night. - At the crossing, vehicles must proceed at walking pace. - Parking spaces for heavy vehicles were redesigned and the lighting was replaced.
## Key facts - What → speed bump and reorganization of the area - Where → Italian-Swiss border crossing at Gaggiolo - Who → Federal Office for Customs and Border Security - Objective → protection of staff, drivers and pedestrians - Rule → passage at walking pace - Other measures → parking spaces redesigned and lighting replaced
The new speed bump installed at the Italian-Swiss border crossing at Gaggiolo is a safety measure. Following reports of delays and traffic disruption recorded in recent days, the UDSC explained the reasons for the decision. The agency specified that the work concerns speed reduction and the reorganization of the customs area.
### The reason for the measure
The measure was adopted after several critical situations had been identified in the customs area. Heavy vehicles, drivers and operational staff move simultaneously near the traffic lanes. Their presence together exposed pedestrians, including workers and drivers involved in customs operations, to risks.
The speed bump was installed and preceded by warning signs. The objective indicated by the UDSC is to reduce the risk of accidents and protect people working or travelling through the area, with particular attention to nighttime hours. The statement therefore links the measure to the daily presence of workers, drivers, operators and pedestrians in the immediate vicinity of the roadway.
### The position of Swiss Customs
The UDSC maintains that the speed bump is appropriate to the characteristics of the road and does not constitute an unjustified obstacle to the flow of vehicles. The reference indicated by the office is the rule already in force at that location: by law, vehicles must in any case proceed at walking pace. For this reason, the structure’s main function is safety and speed reduction, without any substantial change to transit conditions.
The measure is not isolated. The parking spaces intended for heavy vehicles have been redesigned to make vehicle management more orderly and safer. The lighting has also been replaced to ensure better visibility, especially at night. The UDSC presents the package as an overall reorganization of operational spaces and services, with the priority of protecting operators and road users.
The UDSC’s clarification brings together two aspects of the measure: reports concerning traffic and the need to protect those working or travelling through the customs area. The official statement identifies ensuring the greatest possible safety in work activities and movement for all the people who use the border crossing every day as its objective. For those crossing Gaggiolo, the UDSC's communication calls for distinguishing between two aspects: the perception of a slowdown and the traffic rule already in force. Reports from recent days concern traffic disruptions; the authority nevertheless maintains that the new speed bump does not add significant slowdowns compared with the conditions already prescribed. The practical interpretation is therefore that this is a point where speed must already be very low and where slowing down serves to make the coexistence of people and vehicles safer.
### An operational area, not just a lane
The description by Swiss Customs shifts attention from the carriageway alone to the entire border area. Those passing through do not merely encounter a feature on the road: heavy vehicles, drivers, customs personnel and pedestrians operate in the same space. For staff and drivers involved in customs operations, the risk identified by the source arises precisely from the need to move near the lanes.
| Aspect | UDSC indication | |---|---| | Speed | At that point, vehicles must proceed at walking pace | | Presence in the area | Heavy vehicles, drivers, operators and pedestrians are present in the same space | | Nighttime hours | Replacing the lighting is intended to improve visibility | | Heavy vehicles | Parking spaces have been redesigned for more orderly and safer management |
For those using the crossing, this means considering the speed bump together with the reorganization of the area. The warning sign precedes the structure; the reduced speed applies at the point where people may be close to the carriageway. The lighting concerns visibility, while the redesign of the parking spaces concerns the management of heavy vehicles. Different functions, united by the goal of safety.
### What changes in how the disruptions are understood
The source does not deny the reported repercussions on traffic. The UDSC specifies, however, that the speed bump should not substantially alter the transit conditions already prescribed. The reference remains the walking pace required by law.
For those working at the crossing, safety also depends on coexistence between commercial flows, customs operations and pedestrian movements. That is why the UDSC presents the speed bump, parking spaces and lighting as parts of the same intervention. ## Operational guidance
The UDSC's communication makes it possible to derive a simple sequence for anyone entering the border-crossing area. It concerns how to cross a space where vehicle traffic intersects with customs operations and the presence of pedestrians.
### Four steps at the border crossing
1. Read the signage in advance. The speed hump is presignaled by warning signs. The signage prepares traffic before the point concerned, without reaching the structure as if it were unexpected.
2. Proceed at walking pace. At the indicated point, the law requires vehicles to proceed at walking pace. This is the most concrete instruction for drivers: the speed hump does not replace the rule, but serves to moderate speed and ensure safety.
3. Consider the entire area. There are not only traffic lanes. The source points to the simultaneous presence of heavy vehicles, drivers, customs operators and pedestrians, with people who may move near the carriageway during customs operations. Anyone crossing must therefore pay attention to these users being present together.
4. Take nighttime conditions into account. The lighting was replaced to ensure better visibility, especially at night. During that period, the work was designed to protect those working or passing through the area; caution remains necessary because people and vehicles share the same space.
### The organization of heavy vehicles
The redesign of the parking spaces for heavy vehicles adds an element to observe during passage. Vehicle management was reorganized with the aim of making the area more orderly and safer. For a driver or an operator, the parking spaces are therefore part of the overall arrangement of the border crossing.
The sequence does not require interpreting the speed hump as a new limit different from the one already in force. It requires connecting signage, walking pace, visibility and the presence of people. This is the logic with which the UDSC presents the work: protecting the working and transit conditions of all users, while the border crossing manages heavy vehicles, drivers, customs operators and pedestrians.
For more information on movements at borders, consult tempi di attesa ai valichi.

item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A new speed bump has been installed on the Swiss side - Queues and delays at the Stabio-Gaggiolo border crossing - Disruptions especially during the early morning hours - Jolts also reported while crossing
## Key facts - Work: new speed bump - Location: near the Stabio-Gaggiolo customs post - Period: past few weeks - Effects: slowdowns, long queues and jolts - Traffic: commuters and heavy vehicles
### The issue reported at the border
The new speed bump installed on the Swiss side of the Stabio-Gaggiolo border crossing is causing inconvenience for cross-border commuters who cross the border every day to go to work. The speed bump, installed near the customs post, has been followed in recent weeks by slowdowns and long queues, especially in the early morning hours.
The reference to the early morning hours indicates the period when the inconvenience is most noticeable. According to the description, this is the same time when commuter traffic is heaviest, and the crossing acts as a bottleneck.
The Italian-Swiss border crossing is described as a bottleneck for commuter traffic. The central point of the report is therefore operational: getting to work takes longer during periods of heavier traffic. The reader emphasizes that even a few extra minutes can translate into significant inconvenience for those who travel the route every day.
The queue is compounded by a different problem, related to how vehicles pass over the structure. A reader reports rather pronounced jolts while crossing, making the passage less easy.
“The passage over the speed bump is accompanied by rather pronounced jolts, making the crossing less easy.”
The request is to verify whether the structure is compatible with the characteristics of the road and with the crossing’s intense daily traffic, including the passage of heavy vehicles. No technical conclusion is formulated, but a concrete problem reported by those who cross the border to go to work is brought to attention. For the cross-border commuter, the new speed bump affects two aspects of the same crossing: the time needed to get through the border crossing and the smoothness of the passage. The reference to heavy vehicles extends the verification from a single vehicle to the entire daily flow, namely the commuter traffic that crosses the border every day. ### What changes for those who cross every day
The report highlights two consequences that the cross-border commuter experiences at the same point, but which should not be confused. The first is temporal: the new speed bump is associated with slowdowns and queues during periods of greatest traffic. The second is physical: crossing produces pronounced jolts. The inconvenience, therefore, is expressed not only as waiting, but also as the quality of the crossing.
| Aspect | Reported element | |---|---| | Timing | Slowdowns and long queues during peak hours | | Moment | Early morning hours | | Crossing | Pronounced jolts of the vehicles | | Flow | Heavy commuter traffic, including the passage of heavy vehicles |
For those who use the border crossing to get to work, this distinction helps them correctly understand the situation. A queue makes the slowdown of the traffic flow visible; a jolt, on the other hand, describes the way the vehicle crosses that point. They are two different signs of the same problem reported after the speed bump was installed.
The practical comparison is between the period before installation and the past few weeks, that is, the period in which the report places the onset of queues, slowdowns, and jolts. This comparison does not require assigning a precise number to the route: it serves to keep travel time and the regularity of the crossing separate, both of which are mentioned by the reader.
### Why the check concerns the entire border crossing
The request is not limited to asking whether the speed bump slows vehicles down. It asks to verify whether the structure is appropriate for the road and the traffic that travels along it every day. The reference to heavy vehicles broadens the point of observation: the proposed verification must consider commuter traffic as a whole, without stopping at a single crossing.
For the cross-border commuter, the practical issue is therefore twofold: reaching the border crossing during the hours when traffic is heaviest and getting over the speed bump without the jolts described. The report remains anchored to the report of the inconveniences and the request to check the adequacy of the structure. ### A practical sequence for reading the problem
For a cross-border commuter crossing Stabio-Gaggiolo, the check can be organized around the four elements already indicated in the report. First: the location. The problem concerns the speed bump installed near the customs post, on the Swiss side of the crossing. Second: the time. The difficulties are reported mainly in the early morning hours and during rush hour. Third: the effect on travel times, with slowdowns and queues. Fourth: the effect on passage, with pronounced jolts.
This sequence avoids mixing different phenomena. A useful description must say whether the observed inconvenience is a queue, a slowdown, a jolt, or a combination of the three. These are the elements that emerge from the text and make it possible to represent the problem without turning a report into a definitive technical assessment.
### What the inspection should verify
The reader's request also indicates the object of the inspection. It is not enough to observe the structure in the abstract: it must be considered in relation to the characteristics of the road, the heavy daily flow at the crossing, and the passage of heavy vehicles. The suitability of the speed bump must therefore be considered together with the place where it was installed and the traffic that passes over it.
For those who have to travel to work across the border, the practical criterion is to keep the two aspects separate: travel time during the busiest periods and the ease of passing over the speed bump. The report focuses attention on inspecting the structure. Following this approach means describing slowdowns, queues, and jolts without adding times, figures, or technical causes not contained in the text.
The point to bring to attention remains limited: the compatibility of the new traffic-calming device with the road and with the flow of traffic that uses the crossing every day. To learn more about the pattern of queues at the borders, consult storico del traffico e delle code ai valichi.

item.title: Cross-border worker taxes Italy Switzerland 2026: practical simulation
item.description: The New Cross-Border Commuter Agreement has been in force since January 1, 2024 Old cross-border commuters: exemption of €7'500 and transitional period 2024–2033 New cross-border commuters: allowance
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The New Frontier Workers Agreement has been in force since January 1, 2024 - Old frontier workers: €7'500 exemption and 2024–2033 transitional period - New frontier workers: €10'000 tax-free allowance - IRPEF 2026: 23%, 33% and 43%
## Key facts - Signature → December 23, 2020 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Italy-Switzerland Convention → 9 March 1976 - AD/AC → 1.1% with cap at CHF 148'200 - LPP → 7–18% by age group, from 25 years
For those looking for cross-border taxes Italy Switzerland 2026 practical simulation, the date to be set is 23 December 2020: on that day the New Cross-border Workers Agreement was signed. The agreement is in force from 1 January 2024 and the Italian ratification is Law 83 of 13 June 2023. If the search uses the expression new tax agreement 2026, the correct date therefore remains 2024.
### The dates that separate the regimes The threshold indicated for old cross-border workers is 17 July 2023. Those who were already such before that date are old cross-border workers. An exemption of €7,500 is foreseen for them, together with a transitional regime valid from 2024 to 2033 and exclusive Swiss taxation.
For new cross-border commuters, from 2024, taxation will be concurrent. Switzerland applies the withholding tax provided for in the agreement; Italy taxes income after the €10,000 allowance and recognizes the Swiss tax credit. In the 730 form, the credit for income produced abroad is managed in part G.
### The fiscal and contribution perimeter The Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Agreement was signed on 9 March 1976. Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA.
For the Italian IRPEF from 2026, the source indicates 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000 and 43% above €50,000. The rule is reported in Law 199/2025, article 1, paragraph 3. For incomes 2024–2025 the reference indicated is 23%, 35% and 43%.
Tax rates, including withholding tax, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At federal level they are administered by AFC/ESTV and the cantonal tax administrations; UFAS does not determine these rates and BFS collects statistical data, but does not set them. In the Swiss pay slip, AVS/AI/IPG is worth 5.3% for the employee, AD/AC 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148'200, LAINF 0.7–1.5% and LPP 7–18% for the age group from 25 years. ## Practical simulation: comparing scenarios
A simulation for a frontier worker in the Canton of Ticino must first distinguish the date on which they became subject to the regime. The year 2026 does not erase this distinction: it becomes the reference year for Italian IRPEF rates when the position entails taxation in Italy. The first comparison, therefore, is not between isolated percentages, but between tax status and reference year.
### The first row to fill in | Scenario | Rule to enter | Check to perform | |---|---|---| | Old frontier worker | €7'500 exemption, 2024–2033 transitional period and exclusive taxation in Switzerland | Do not apply the €10'000 tax-free allowance | | New frontier worker | Swiss withholding tax, Italian tax on income above €10'000 and a tax credit for Swiss tax | Do not treat it as a position taxed only in Switzerland | | Italian IRPEF 2026 | 23% up to €28'000, 33% from €28'001 to €50'000, 43% above €50'000 | Do not use the 35% provided for the second income bracket in 2024–2025 |
In a hypothetical scenario, a frontier worker who already had that status before July 17, 2023 remains in the first row even if the simulation concerns 2026. The new year does not turn the transitional regime into that of new frontier workers. For those who instead fall under the second row, the sequence must keep the Swiss withholding tax, Italian income after the allowance and the tax credit for Swiss tax separate. This is the step used to handle double taxation; in the 730 form, the relevant section is Section G.
### Separating taxes, contributions, and insurance The result of the simulation should not be read as a single percentage. The Swiss items are distinct in nature: AVS/AI/IPG is listed at 5.3% for the employee; AD/AC is 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148'200; LAINF ranges from 0.7% to 1.5%; LPP varies from 7% to 18% by age group, starting at age 25. Keeping them separate prevents contributions and IRPEF from being automatically added together as if they were the same withholding.
For a frontier worker with a G permit, LAMal must also be kept on a separate line. LAMal is health insurance, not a tax on health, and G frontier workers have the right to opt. The adult deductibles indicated by the source range from CHF 300 to CHF 2500: they differ from the €10'000 tax allowance and must not be entered in the same step of the calculation. ## Operational checklist for 2026
To turn the rules into a practical simulation, it is advisable to follow a fixed order. The procedure does not require inventing amounts: it uses only the date of the regime, the tax year and the items indicated in the source.
### Five checks before the result 1. Classify the situation. Note whether you were already a frontier worker before July 17, 2023. This date separates the regime for old frontier workers from that for new ones. For the first group, consider the €7'500 exemption and the 2024–2033 transitional period; for the second, consider the €10'000 tax-free allowance.
2. Set the tax year. If the simulation concerns 2026, use the IRPEF brackets of 23% up to €28'000, 33% from €28'001 to €50'000 and 43% above €50'000. For 2024–2025 income, note instead the values 23%, 35% and 43%.
3. Separate the two tax stages for new frontier workers. Keep the withholding applied in Switzerland distinct from Italian taxation on income after the €10'000 tax-free allowance. The credit for Swiss tax, in Form 730, must be handled in section G. If the position concerns old frontier workers, retain the exclusive Swiss taxation of the transitional regime.
4. Read the Swiss items without combining them into a single rate. Record AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% for the employee, AD/AC at 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148'200, LAINF at 0.7–1.5% and LPP at 7–18% by age bracket from age 25.
5. Separate LAMal from taxation. If you have a G permit, consider the right of option for G frontier workers and keep the adult deductible separate, between CHF 300 and CHF 2500. Do not call LAMal a health tax: the source identifies it as health insurance.
The allocation of responsibilities is clear: federal and cantonal laws set withholding-tax rates, while AFC/ESTV administers them at federal level and the cantonal tax administrations operate at cantonal level. UFAS does not set tax rates, and BFS is responsible for collecting statistical data, not determining them. To apply these indications to salary, taxes and contributions, use calcolatore fiscale.

## TL;DR - Sunday, April 11, 2027: start and finish in Angera - Three lakes and eight municipalities in the project - Approximately 2.000 runners estimated for the first edition - Economic impact between 600mila and 750mila euro
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Event | Lakes Marathon | | Promoter | Varese Welcome Foundation | | Presentation | TTG Travel Experience of Rimini | | Date | Sunday 11 April 2027 | | Departure and arrival | Angera | | Path | Three lakes and eight municipalities | | Tests | Marathon, half marathon and 10 kilometers | | Valued Attendees | About 2,000 runners |
### The project presented in Rimini Sunday 11 April 2027 Angera will be the starting and finishing point of the Maratona dei Laghi, a new event promoted by the Varese Welcome Foundation. The project combines three events: a marathon, a half marathon and a 10 kilometer race.
The initiative was presented at the TTG Travel Experience in Rimini, among the initiatives hosted in the Lombardy Region stand. For the Varese Welcome Foundation, this is the first major sports competition promoted by the Varese Welcome Foundation. The proposal involves eight municipalities and three lakes in the Varese area.
The organizers aim to transform the race into an opportunity to discover the area, involving accommodation facilities, restaurateurs, commercial activities and tourist services. The event is thus proposed not only as a competition, but also as a project capable of linking the carrying out of the tests to the presence of visitors in the area.
For the promoters, the choice of those who run concerns both the test and the place to experience before and after the event. The "More than a Marathon" formula is based on this idea, also designed for the athletes' companions, who will be able to use the trip to stop for a few days in the Varese area.
For the first edition, the organizers estimate around two thousand runners and direct economic benefits of between 600 thousand and 750 thousand euros. These are the numbers associated with the initial scope of the project, which combines the sporting offer with the promotion of the territory.
The departure and arrival in Angera give the city a central role in the design of the event. Around this point a project is developed that involves Ispra, Brebbia, Cadrezzate, Travedona Monate, Biandronno, Bardello with Malgesso and Bregano and Ranco. The event is therefore designed on a broader territorial dimension than just the starting municipality. ## Sports tourism and economic impact
### Estimates for the first edition
The figures released for the first edition distinguish between the three distances and also include the people accompanying the participants. The total includes approximately two thousand runners: 500 are expected for the marathon, 800 for the half marathon and 700 for the 10-kilometer race. They would be joined by approximately 1.500 accompanying persons.
| Item | Estimate | |---|---:| | Total runners | Approximately 2.000 | | Marathon participants | 500 | | Half-marathon participants | 800 | | Participants in the 10-kilometer race | 700 | | Accompanying persons | Approximately 1.500 | | Average stay | 1,8 nights | | Daily spending | 120 euro | | Direct economic impact | Between 600mila and 750mila euro |
The organizers' calculations are based on average stays of 1,8 nights, with daily spending of 120 euro. In the presentation release, the total direct economic impact is estimated at between 600mila and 750mila euro. The figure concerns the first edition and is presented as an estimate of the impact linked to the event.
To support sports tourism, the Camera di Commercio di Varese launched the call for applications “Sport&Stay: extend your vacation”. The presentation release indicates grants of up to 200 euro per night, intended to encourage athletes to extend their stay beyond the race days.
The measure is paired with the marathon project as a tool to support a longer stay than participation in the races alone. The reference to athletes concerns extending their stay beyond the race days, while the economic estimates also include the accompanying persons listed by the organizers.
For subsequent editions, the stated goal is to reach three thousand registered participants. This figure is not a forecast for the debut, which remains set at approximately two thousand runners, but the target cited for the continuation of the event. The first edition therefore comes with a growth outlook already defined in the project.
Mauro Vitiello, president of Fondazione Varese Welcome and the Camera di Commercio di Varese, links the initiative to sports tourism and the promotion of the area.
> Mauro Vitiello, president of Fondazione Varese Welcome and the Camera di Commercio di Varese, states: «La Maratona dei Laghi represents an important showcase and a fundamental piece in continuing to develop sports tourism». Vitiello adds that the event will help promote the area by bringing sport, nature and hospitality together. ## The course and the three races
### From the shore of Lake Maggiore to Lake Varese The sporting program scheduled for Sunday, April 11, 2027, is divided into three distances. The marathon is 42,195 kilometers long and features 280 meters of elevation gain. The half marathon is 21,097 kilometers long, with 124 meters of elevation gain. These two races are joined by a 10-kilometer race.
The longest distance will start in Angera and follow the shores of Lake Maggiore. The course will then continue toward Lake Monate, reached between the thirteenth and sixteenth kilometers, and will arrive in the Lake Varese area between the twentieth and twenty-third kilometers.
The organizers' presentation lays out the course in relation to the three bodies of water involved in the project: Lake Maggiore at the beginning, Lake Monate in the section from the thirteenth to the sixteenth kilometer, and Lake Varese in the section from the twentieth to the twenty-third kilometer. These are the geographical reference points of the marathon given in the presentation.
The list of municipalities involved includes Angera, Ispra, Brebbia, Cadrezzate, Travedona Monate, Biandronno, Bardello con Malgesso e Bregano and Ranco. The event therefore involves eight municipalities, with Angera identified as the start and finish location. The project thus maintains a direct link between the sporting course and the Varese lakes area.
The three races have different characteristics: the marathon features the greatest distance and elevation gain; the half marathon offers a shorter course and an elevation gain of 124 meters; the 10-kilometer race completes the program. The source does not assign a specific route among the lakes to the two shorter races, while it describes the marathon course in detail.
For subsequent editions, the organizers' stated goal is to reach three thousand registrants. The first event remains the one scheduled for April 11, 2027, with the start and finish in Angera and a program consisting of a marathon, half marathon and 10-kilometer race. Growth to three thousand registrants is instead indicated as an objective for subsequent events.

item.title: Is working in Switzerland still worthwhile?
item.description: In September 2026 Swiss unemployment is at 3% In one year, the number of unemployed increases by 5,4% In the second quarter, employment grows by 2% Publication
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In September 2026, Swiss unemployment is at 3% - Over one year, the number of unemployed people increases by 5,4% - In the second quarter, employment increases by 2%
## Key facts - SECO publication → October 6, 2026 - Unemployed in September → 140.480 - Registered jobseekers → 237.244 - UST publication → August 27, 2026 - Jobs in the second quarter → 5,698 million - Growth in jobs → 111.800 positions
On October 6, 2026, SECO published the latest data on the Swiss labor market, painting a picture that combines higher unemployment than in the previous year with job growth.
In September, 140.480 people were registered as unemployed, with an unemployment rate of 3%. Compared with August, the number fell by 1.064, equivalent to 0,8%. The comparison with September 2025, however, shows an increase of 7.247 people, equal to 5,4%. Once adjusted for seasonal effects, the rate reaches 3,1%.
SECO also considers a broader indicator: in September, 237.244 people were registered with the regional employment offices as unemployed or as other registered jobseekers, adjusted for seasonal variations, with a rate of 5%. This total exceeds that of unemployed people alone because it also includes those seeking a new job without being counted as unemployed according to administrative criteria.
### The market that continues to create jobs
The UST statistics published on August 27, 2026, describe a different trajectory on the employment front. In the second quarter of the year, jobs in Switzerland reached 5,698 million, with 111.800 more jobs than in the same quarter of 2025. The increase amounted to 2% year on year. Services accounted for the main share of the growth, with 98.700 additional jobs; industry and construction added another 13.100.
The combination of these figures prevents a one-sided reading. Companies continue to hire and report difficulties finding qualified personnel, but the number of people without work is higher than a year earlier. For some groups, the market is therefore more competitive, even though total employment has grown.
For Italian workers, interest in Switzerland remains linked to average salaries that are higher than in Italy, the strength of the Swiss economy, and the possibility of living across the border while earning a salary in Swiss francs. However, the latest data suggest that access is not necessarily as straightforward as in the past. In the Canton of Ticino, the number of cross-border workers is showing signs of slowing. This local factor accompanies national job growth and makes it necessary to distinguish between the general trend and the one affecting those seeking work across the border. ## The national labor market is not the same as the Ticino figure
The question of whether working in Switzerland still pays off does not receive an automatic yes or no from the figures. The source confirms the reasons that make the market attractive to many Italians: average salaries higher than in Italy, the strength of the Swiss economy, and the possibility of living across the border while retaining a salary in Swiss francs. But the same picture shows tougher selection for some categories. For a cross-border worker, economic advantage and the likelihood of finding a job are not the same piece of information.
The increase in employment indicates that companies continue to hire, while the rise in the number of unemployed indicates that job hunting may be more competitive for some people. Both things can happen at the same time, and this very overlap is what should be borne in mind when assessing a cross-border career move. The source does not describe a general employment crisis: it does, however, make clear that the market has become more competitive for some categories and that companies report difficulties finding qualified staff. For Italian readers, the useful comparison is therefore between the skills in demand and the opportunities actually available, not between a single national figure.
### Three signals not to confuse
| Signal | Practical interpretation | |---|---| | Year-on-year increase in the number of unemployed | The market is more competitive for some categories | | Growing employment | Companies continue to expand their workforces | | Growth in services | Most of the new jobs are here | | A slowdown among cross-border workers in Ticino | The local signal should be distinguished from the national figure |
An increase in employment throughout Switzerland cannot be taken as the number of open positions in the Canton of Ticino. The source presents the FSO figure as national and does not provide a breakdown for the canton. Likewise, growth in services does not say which professions are involved or what requirements are sought. The slowdown among cross-border workers in Ticino is not accompanied by a quantification or a cause in the text: it therefore cannot be turned into a forecast of future employment.
The scope remains the labor market. The data reported do not provide information on the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation; these topics cannot be inferred from statistics on unemployment and employment. ## A five-step method
The source makes it possible to build a practical assessment without turning statistics into promises. For someone who is a cross-border worker or is considering a job in Canton Ticino, the first check concerns the date to which each number refers.
### Separating dates, territory and skills
1. Separate the sources and dates. Use the SECO release of October 6, 2026, for unemployment and the UST statistics of August 27, 2026, for employment. They are different snapshots: September for the unemployed, second quarter for jobs.
2. Distinguish the national level from the local level. The 5,698 million jobs describe Switzerland. They should not be read as available positions in Canton Ticino. For the canton, the source only reports a slowdown in the number of cross-border workers.
3. Look at the structure of growth. Services added 98.700 jobs, while industry and construction added 13.100. The figure helps show where the increase is concentrated, but the source does not indicate specific professions or requirements.
4. Compare your profile with the demand for qualifications. Companies continue to hire and report difficulties finding qualified personnel. The question to ask is whether the skills required by companies coincide with those available, as the same data suggests.
5. Keep the signals separate. The increase in unemployed people and the growth in jobs do not cancel each other out. The former describes a greater presence of people looking for work; the latter shows expansion of staff. The choice should therefore be based on actual opportunities, not on a single percentage.
This method avoids two opposite conclusions: thinking that Switzerland no longer offers opportunities or that every job search is easy. The source supports neither conclusion. For the cross-border worker, the practical point is to use the statistics as an initial filter: check the period, territory, sector and skills. The available material does not allow details to be added about individual opportunities in Canton Ticino beyond those indicated.
If the goal is to move from the general picture to the search for opportunities consistent with your profile, consult annunci di lavoro.

## TL;DR - Starting November 15, 2026, MA*GA opens its new season - “Jago. Exposed Bodies” from November 15, 2026 to April 4, 2027 - “Water” at Palazzo Lombardia from November 11, 2026 - “According to Leopardi” until December 8, 2026
## Key facts - Place → MA*GA Museum of Gallarate - Central exhibition → «Jago. Bodies exposed" - Curator → Tommaso Zijno - Reorganization → «The museum of currents» - Third project → «Secondo Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art" - Festival → Duemilalibri - Installation in Milan → «Water» - Tickets → TicketOne and MA*GA ticket office
### Three projects for the season On November 15, 2026, the MA*GA Museum in Gallarate opens a new exhibition season divided into three projects. The programming explores, through different approaches, the corporeal dimension, the social function of the museum institution and the link between literature and visual arts.
At the center is «Jago. Exposed bodies», exhibition curated by Tommaso Zijno and dedicated to the work of the sculptor Jago. The project puts his works in dialogue with those of Adolfo Wildt, Emilio Vedova, Salvatore Scarpitta and Marinella Pirelli. The exhibition will be accompanied by the rearrangement of the museum's collections through «The museum of currents», curated by Emma Zanella and Alessandro Castiglioni.
The third proposal is «According to Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art", included in the program of Duemilalibri, the book and author festival of Gallarate. The exhibition brings back to MA*GA a nucleus of works linked to the relationship between the poetry of Giacomo Leopardi and the visual arts, with a contemporary reading of visual poetry.
The program therefore distributes the three initiatives between contemporary art, twentieth-century history and new interpretations of the museum's heritage. «Iago. Exposed bodies" and "The museum of currents" are scheduled from 15 November 2026 to 4 April 2027, while "Secondo Leopardi" is scheduled from 15 November to 8 December 2026.
The proposal does not end in the spaces of Gallarate. The project dedicated to Jago also includes a second intervention in Milan, at Palazzo Lombardia, where the installation «Water» will be presented. The two exhibitions are autonomous, but build a journey between Milan and Gallarate around the artist's research.
Tickets can be purchased in advance on TicketOne and at the MA*GA ticket office. The museum thus presents a season built on three different readings, united by the desire to connect contemporary works, memory of the twentieth century and the heritage of the collection. ### The body as surface and conflict The project “Jago. Exposed Bodies” begins with a comparison between Jago’s practice and that of four artists belonging to different periods and artistic languages. Jago, born in 1987, is placed alongside Adolfo Wildt, Emilio Vedova, Salvatore Scarpitta and Marinella Pirelli to construct a dialogue spanning more than a century of artistic research.
The exhibition is organized around two themes. The first is stripping away, understood as a gesture capable of revealing what lies beneath the surface. The second concerns war, presented as an extreme situation in which the body becomes a battleground. The itinerary therefore uses the human figure to address questions related to matter, violence and collective responsibility.
The resonances among the works connect Jago’s practice to Vedova’s gestural energy, Scarpitta’s material approach and Pirelli’s reflections on the political body. The comparison with Wildt takes on particular significance: like Jago, the sculptor used marble to bring out fragility, spirituality and pain.
Tommaso Zijno’s curatorial approach thus presents a reading of the body not limited to its physical dimension. Through the works brought together at MA*GA, the body becomes a tool for reflecting on power, violence, mysticism and collective responsibility. The chronological distance between the artists does not eliminate the connections, but makes it possible to follow transformations and continuities in artistic research.
### A collection read through currents “The Museum of Currents” instead stems from work on the historical archive of the Civic Gallery of Modern Art of Gallarate and from an analysis of the museographic concepts formulated by Silvio Zanella, the museum’s founder, between 1972 and 2000. The project is part of the activities of the Italia 2050 Research Center, founded in 2023 by Museo MAGA and the Lombardy Region.
Zanella envisioned a museum capable of telling the story not only of the development of artistic languages, but also of humanity, society and civilization in every era through those languages. The new installation takes up and updates this vision, abandoning a linear reading of art history in favor of a journey made up of returns, ruptures, accelerations and transformations.
There will also be a focus on research investigating the links between art, nature and ecology. The collection will thus be presented as an interweaving of currents and transitions, reinterpreted through relationships that go beyond chronological order alone. ### Leopardi between words and images «According to Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art» completes the MA*GA program with an exhibition scheduled from November 15 to December 8, 2026, as part of Duemilalibri, Gallarate's book and author festival.
The project begins with a body of works that became part of the MA*GA collection following «Pages and Pages. 1798 / 1998 tribute to Giacomo Leopardi». In 1998, Gino Gini conceived the exhibition to mark the bicentenary of the birth of the poet from Recanati. That body is now being presented again through a contemporary interpretation that brings together visual poetry and artistic practices.
Among the artists featured in the exhibition are Tomaso Binga, Mirella Bentivoglio and Lamberto Pignotti. The relationship with Leopardi is therefore explored not only through literature, but also through works that engage with the visual dimension of the word and the possibilities of the image. The exhibition connects the museum's holdings with a contemporary reinterpretation of the poet from Recanati.
### The itinerary between Gallarate and Milan The program dedicated to Jago also extends to Palazzo Lombardia. From November 11, 2026, to January 10, 2027, the Milan venue will host «Water», an installation that juxtaposes the solidity of matter with the flow of time.
The Milan project and the Gallarate exhibition remain independent, but are presented as parts of a shared itinerary centered on the artist's research. The link between the two venues adds a second stop dedicated to Jago to the MA*GA season, distinct from the comparison between his works and those of Wildt, Vedova, Scarpitta and Pirelli.
The dates make it possible to follow a varied program. On November 15, 2026, «Jago. Bodies on display», «The museum of currents» and «According to Leopardi» will open in Gallarate, while Palazzo Lombardia will already have opened the «Water» project on November 11, 2026. The exhibition dedicated to Leopardi will end on December 8, 2026; the other two MA*GA initiatives will continue until April 4, 2027, and the Milan installation until January 10, 2027.
For access to the exhibitions, tickets can be purchased in advance on TicketOne and at the MA*GA ticket office. The museum thus rounds out the season with a program spread across Gallarate and Milan, keeping the individual projects distinct while connecting them through the themes of the body, the collection, and the relationship between poetry and the visual arts.

### The concert
On Sunday 25 October 2026, at 6 pm, Uto Ughi will be the protagonist at the Teatro Condominio Vittorio Gassman in Gallarate, for an event dedicated to great classical music. The famous violinist will return to the city's stage one year after his previous concert.
He will be accompanied by the Virtuosi del Lemene, together with soloists Glauco Bertagnin on violin and Walter Zampiron on flute. The presence of the two musicians will complement that of the ensemble in a concert conceived as a dialogue between soloists and orchestra.
The programme will be dedicated to Antonio Vivaldi and Johann Sebastian Bach. The evening will bring together some of the most famous and evocative compositions of the Baroque repertoire, in a selection that will highlight elegance and virtuosity.
Ughi's return brings one of Italy's best-known international performers back to Gallarate. The programme and the participation of the Virtuosi del Lemene will help to highlight the legacy of classical music, creating a high-profile event.
The event therefore stems from the meeting between the famous violinist, the ensemble that will accompany him and the two soloists chosen for the evening. The stage of the Teatro Condominio will thus host a musical journey focused on Vivaldi and Bach, with the violin and flute included in the programme dedicated to the Baroque repertoire. ## The return after a year
### The promise kept
For Gallarate, the concert marks the return of an artist already known to the city. During last year’s event, Uto Ughi had met the city’s audience at Teatro Condominio, leaving open the possibility of performing again.
The promise is now fulfilled with the concert on October 25. Councillor for Culture and Educational Activities Claudia Mazzetti linked the new event to the positive relationship the violinist had built with the venue, the audience and the city.
“His return, after last year’s concert, gives me great pleasure: he had greatly appreciated the theatre, the audience and the welcome from the city of Gallarate. I am pleased that he kept his promise.”
In Mazzetti’s comments, the evening is presented as an event of the highest calibre. The councillor also identifies two aims associated with the event: to showcase Uto Ughi, considered one of the world’s greatest violinists, and to bring classical music, described as a heritage, back to the forefront.
With this event, Teatro Condominio continues its cultural journey, after hosting initiatives in different genres in recent years. The venue has alternated between drama and music, with the aim of broadening its offering and also making room again for the great classical repertoire.
The new evening with Ughi thus fits within this path already outlined by the source. The previous meeting with the audience and the welcome received by the violinist are the elements that accompanied his return to the stage in Gallarate, alongside the desire to devote space to classical music. ## The event in Gallarate
### Date, venue and tickets
The next event is scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at 18, at the Teatro Condominio “Vittorio Gassman” in Gallarate, at the corner of via Sironi and via Verdi. Tickets can be purchased through Ticketone.
The venue will host Uto Ughi together with the Virtuosi del Lemene. Also taking the stage will be Glauco Bertagnin on violin and Walter Zampiron on flute, according to the lineup planned for the concert. The formation has been presented as part of the program built around Baroque music.
The audience will enjoy an evening dedicated to Antonio Vivaldi and Johann Sebastian Bach. The announced program explores some of the best-known and most fascinating works in the Baroque repertoire and connects the presence of the soloists with that of the ensemble.
The structure of the concert was conceived as a dialogue between soloists and orchestra. The roles indicated for the evening are therefore distinct: Uto Ughi will be the featured violinist, Glauco Bertagnin will join the program, also on violin, Walter Zampiron will perform on flute, and the Virtuosi del Lemene will accompany the renowned violinist.
The October 25 event will thus bring together at the same venue the program dedicated to Vivaldi and Bach, the announced musicians, and Ughi’s return after last year’s concert. item.description: 2026 Furia Award to Enrico Giovannini Economist and statistician, professor at Roma Tor Vergata He was Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT ASviS founded
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Furia Award 2026 to Enrico Giovannini - Economist and statistician, lecturer at Roma Tor Vergata - He was Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT - ASviS founded in 2016
## Key facts - Award → Premio Ecologia Città di Varese – Salvatore Furia 2026 - Recipient → Enrico Giovannini - Profile → economist and statistician - Positions → two-time minister, Chief Statistician of the OECD, president of ISTAT - Teaching → University of Rome Tor Vergata and National School of Administration - Agenda → United Nations 2030 Agenda - ASviS → founded in 2016 - Origin → Award founded by Salvatore Furia in 1973
The Premio Ecologia Città di Varese – Salvatore Furia 2026 is being awarded this year to Enrico Giovannini. The committee's decision concerns a figure who has transformed awareness of the environmental crisis into a reflection on the responsibilities of society, institutions and the economic system.
Giovannini is an economist and statistician. At the University of Rome Tor Vergata, he teaches Economic Statistics and Analysis and Policies for Sustainable Development as a full professor, in addition to teaching at the National School of Administration. Over the course of his career, he has been a two-time minister, Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT.
He is co-founder and scientific director of the Italian Alliance for Sustainable Development, ASviS. The founding of the Alliance in 2016 represents a key milestone in a commitment to promoting the United Nations 2030 Agenda and a vision of development capable of bringing together the environmental, economic and social dimensions.
### The committee's rationale
The choice recognizes the scientific, institutional and public-outreach work through which Giovannini has placed sustainable development at the center of public debate. Well-being, in the perspective highlighted by the committee, does not coincide with economic growth alone: it includes quality of life, social cohesion, the protection of natural resources and the opportunities left to future generations.
### Salvatore Furia's legacy
The award thus recalls the figure of its founder, the naturalist and science communicator Salvatore Furia, who in 1973 linked knowledge of nature with education and the growth of the community. According to Nicoletta San Martino, councillor of the Municipality of Varese with responsibility for Environmental Protection, Social Sustainability and the Circular Economy, Furia's teaching instilled in young people a tangible sense of responsibility toward their local area:
> “To many young people, in addition to knowledge of nature, Furia passed on the ability to observe nature, learn about their own area and feel responsible for protecting it.”
The 2026 rationale therefore fits into his idea of environmental culture: understanding natural balances, recognizing human responsibility and turning awareness into responsible behavior. The choice links the recipient's profile to the tradition of the award: from knowledge of nature to collective responsibility, without separating the environment, society and the economy. The committee considers this transition consistent with Furia's cultural legacy. ## Sustainability as a lens
For the cross-border reader, the scope of the news is clear-cut. The source does not mention the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation. It therefore provides no deadlines, amounts or procedures for those who work across the border: its subject is a cultural recognition and the way collective well-being is defined.
### From growth to well-being
What makes Giovannini’s choice broad in scope is moving beyond the separation between environmental and social policies. Sustainability is not described solely as the protection of natural resources. It also requires understanding how opportunities are distributed, who bears the costs of transformations and whether people can live in dignified conditions.
| Dimension | Framing indicated by the source | | Development | Not just economic growth, but quality of life and social cohesion | | Environment | Protection of ecosystems and natural resources | | Society | Combating poverty and inequalities, with inclusive and resilient communities | | Future | Opportunities for future generations and shared responsibilities |
This approach is the core of the integral ecology referred to in the recognition. The environmental crisis and the social crisis are not treated as separate problems: the former concerns natural balances, the latter the dignity of people and the conditions of the most vulnerable communities. Sustainability, therefore, requires a vision capable of connecting economic choices, institutions, social behavior and the protection of nature.
ASviS translates this perspective into the dissemination of the 2030 Agenda and its 17 Goals. The program combines the fight against poverty, the reduction of inequalities, the protection of ecosystems, the adoption of responsible practices in production and consumption, and the development of more inclusive and resilient societies. It is not a catalogue of separate topics: the source stresses their interdependence.
For those reading from a border region, the value of the news therefore lies in the lens it offers, not in a change to working life. The award invites us to ask whether a public decision considers the environment, economy and society together, and whether it distributes opportunities and costs fairly. These are the questions that connect Giovannini’s work to the institutional responsibility highlighted by the committee. ## Four steps for reading the award
The source makes it possible to follow a simple sequence to understand why the 2026 award is presented as the culmination of a cultural journey. There is no need to add tax or employment data: the content revolves around the connections between knowledge, culture, health, the economy and institutions.
### 1. Follow the path of the awards
The first step is to observe the series of the last five years through the recognitions mentioned. In 2022, Barbara Gallavotti represented the role of science communication in making complex knowledge accessible. In 2023, Michelangelo Pistoletto brought the relationship between culture, creativity, society and the planet into the award. In 2025, Ilaria Capua, with the vision of Salute Circolare, connected human health, animal health and environmental health, together with the impact of social behavior, the economy, law and information.
### 2. Identify the next step
The second step consists of reading Giovannini as the institutional and economic culmination of the sequence. After scientific knowledge, culture and health, the recognition focuses on how states regulate collective life, distribute opportunities and plan for the future. This is why the profile of an economist and statistician is included in an award dedicated to ecology.
### 3. Use the 17 Goals as a map
The third step is to verify the presence of the dimensions indicated by Agenda 2030: poverty and inequalities, ecosystems, responsible production and consumption, inclusive and resilient societies. The map serves to avoid reducing ecology to the mere conservation of nature and to recognize that environmental policies have social consequences.
### 4. Bring knowledge back to the community
The final step returns to Salvatore Furia’s method. Knowledge of natural balances must become awareness, and awareness must translate into responsible behavior. This is why education is part of sustainability: it does not remain specialized knowledge, but becomes a common heritage and involves society.
Read in this sequence, the news offers the public of Varese and readers beyond the borders a criterion for following the environmental debate without separating it from social and economic issues. The 2026 Premio Furia is not presented solely as an individual recognition, but as a stage in a culture of care.

### The comeback after the first set
Erreci Busto Arsizio turned the midweek round into another leg of his clean sweep: Marchiaro's team beat Ferraro Smi Roma 3-1, after losing the first set, and remains full-scoring in the women's A2 championship.
For Futura Volley Giovani it is the third league game and the third three-point victory. After Perugia and Marsala, Rome also goes to the carpet: the whites climb to 9 and remain paired at Costa Volpino, waiting for the Altafratte match. The next opponent will be Costa Volpino at the Soevis Arena, on Sunday 18 October.
The Ferraro Smi starts better and wins the first set for 22-25, with Perovic in evidence; Edinara, returned from the injury, still offers a good contribution by scoring 5 points. Busto reacts in the second partial, won 25-22, with the Brazilian protagonist of the attacks from place 2. The finale also features Marconato, who was instrumental in repelling the last attempt at a Roman comeback.
The 25-22 is repeated in the third set. Šiftar grows with the passing of exchanges, while Cosi becomes impassable on the wall. Rome, having failed to return to the game, loses consistency and leaves the Futura free field in the fourth quarter, closed 25-14 with another dominant test of the Slovenian crusher.
Marchiaro explained that the team expected an aggressive Roma, but had started the contracted race, almost as if Busto had to lead the game. The coach then reminded the team of the need to start from scratch each time, without looking at the standings, and to conquer one set at a time. ### The numbers that explain the 3-1
The box score highlights a Futura side powered primarily by its attacks and blocking. The top scorer is Šiftar, with 24 points and 61% in attack. Edinara finishes with 19 points, 40% in attack and 2 blocks. Emma Cagnin, voted MVP of the evening, adds 16 points with 42% in attack and 47% perfect reception.

item.description: Le Azalee Calcio leave the field on Via Pradisera.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Le Azalee Calcio leave the field on Via Pradisera. - The tender for the area received no bids. - Ugo Tomaselli denounces a substantial exclusion. - The Municipality points to the expired concession.
## Key facts - Location → field on Via Pradisera, Gallarate - Club → Azalee Calcio - President → Ugo Tomaselli - Tender → no bids - Athletics cage → nearly 25mila euro
Azalee Calcio announced on social media the return of the keys to the field on Via Pradisera, in Gallarate, after decades at the facility. The matter revolves around the tender for the concession of the area, which received no bids, but the two sides interpret it differently: the club speaks of being effectively ousted; the Municipality instead points to the expiry of the concession and the lack of conditions for a simple extension.
In the post published on social media, the club called the procedure improper and recalled its role in promoting women’s football, claiming to have made Gallarate known throughout Italy since 1980.
> “After fifty years, we’re out,” sums up president Ugo Tomaselli.
The president explained that he had waited for the new tender while assessing the work needed to continue operations at the facility. The possibilities considered included replacing the floodlights with LED fixtures and resurfacing the grass pitch.
### The tender and the required conditions
According to Tomaselli, the lack of participation was also due to the obligations imposed on the future concessionaire. Among the required works was a cage for athletics throwing events, whose cost the club estimated at nearly 25mila euro.
Until then, Atletica Gallaratese had used the spaces, paying Azalee sublease rent. Under the new arrangement, the structure would have had to be built. The president says that Atletica was unwilling to contribute and that Azalee could not bear the cost alone. The tender therefore received no bids.
After the bidding closed, the Municipality sent the club a Pec requesting the return of the facility. Tomaselli explained that neither requests for an extension nor the possibility of talks between the clubs had been enough to avoid the handover. The return of the keys therefore marks Azalee’s departure from the field on Via Pradisera, but leaves unresolved the dispute over management of the concession and the significance of the tender that received no bids. The Municipality's reconstruction starts from the facility's corporate history and does not coincide with that of Azalee. Mayor Andrea Cassani, who initially intervened by commenting on the post published by the company, distinguishes between the previous company awarded the concession and Azalee 1980, chaired by Ugo Tomaselli.
According to Cassani, the entity that today claims continuity with the Gallarate team would have a new corporate name and a new tax code. The transfer between the two companies, the mayor maintains, would never have been formally communicated to the Municipality. Azalee 1980 would have continued to play on the field on the basis of an agreement with the old company, but without an official communication to the administration.
Cassani also points to the financial situation of the previous management. According to what the mayor told VareseNews, the first company awarded the concession would have a debt crystallized as of 2023 amounting to 23,000 euros. The administration includes this figure in its own account of the dealings related to the facility.
The decisive point, however, remains the tender published to award the area. The mayor maintains that neither the old Azalee nor the new company took part in it. On the basis of this circumstance, he rejects the idea that the Municipality drove the team out: in the administration's view, the concessions had expired and no one had submitted a proposal to obtain the area again.
As for the extension, Cassani denies that it can be granted. Sports Councillor Claudia Mazzetti, by contrast, defends the Municipality's actions: she maintains that alternatives had been offered and that the situation had been explained clearly.
For the administration, the issue of the cage for athletics throwing events also remains open. Le Azalee had listed it among the obstacles to participating, since the project would have entailed an investment intended for another discipline. Cassani attributes the decision not to build it to the company and hypothesizes that, if the area is assigned again, the work could be the responsibility of another party.
The positions therefore remain far apart over the origin of the split. The company considers the request to hand back the area the outcome of an improper procedure; the Municipality links it to the expiry of the concession, the tender with no bids, and the absence of the conditions for an extension. The rest of the story mainly concerns the continuity of the Azalee's sporting activities after leaving the field on via Pradisera. The club had two women's teams and a men's team. After the keys were handed back, president Tomaselli explained that only the men's team will play at Majno. As for training, however, a solution still needs to be found.
The consequence described by the club therefore concerns not only the availability of the facility, but also the possibility of keeping the various teams organized. The men's team has an indicated destination, while no arrangement has been found for training activities. The Azalee also lament the loss of the teams, directly linking the abandonment of the field to the difficulty of continuing the sporting project.
### The closed field and the future of the area
Meanwhile, the historic football field remains padlocked. The return requested by the Municipality thus had an immediate effect on access to the facility, without the discussions between the clubs leading to the extension requested by the Azalee or to the opening of the meeting proposed by the president.
From an administrative standpoint, the Municipality confirms that the concession cannot be extended. The future of the area is thus tied to a new award, mentioned by Cassani as the possibility through which another party could build the cage needed for athletics throwing events. The work therefore remains associated with the subsequent management of the facility and not with the continuation of the Azalee's activities.
The situation leaves two distinct aspects open. On the one hand, there is the management of the area, which received no offers in the tender and has the field closed. On the other hand, there is sporting continuity, which for the Azalee means moving the men's team to Majno and seeking spaces for training. The source does not describe a new concessionaire or an already defined solution for the women's teams. The firm point, instead, is the one indicated by the Municipality: no extension for the expired concession and the prospect that any new concessionaire could take care of the athletics facility.
