item.title: OCST history: from 1919 to protecting cross-border commuters in Ticino
item.description: The Chamber of Labor was founded in 1902.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Chamber of Labour was established in 1902. - OCST was founded on May 18, 1919. - The statutes were adopted on November 16 in Bellinzona. - Many cross-border workers unionized during the boom.
## Key facts - Origin → workers' societies founded on solidarity and mutual aid - Economic turning point → Gotthard Railway, 1882 - Chamber of Labour → 1902 - OCST → May 18, 1919 - Statutes → November 16, 1919, Bellinzona - Magazine → Il Lavoro, since 1920 - Secretary → don Luigi Del Pietro, since September 1, 1929 - Cross-border workers → many were unionized during the economic boom
### From solidarity to founding Around the middle of the nineteenth century, in a poor Canton Ticino where agriculture and pastoralism were the main activities, the first small workers' societies based on solidarity and mutual aid were established. The construction of the Gotthard Railway in 1882 changed the canton's economy: agriculture began to decline, while factories, tourism and services appeared in the towns. According to the account presented in January 2021, this turning point was the result of a long social transformation.
The workers' association movement was promoted by Italian immigrants and Ticinese emigrants, who had encountered more advanced social conditions abroad. At the end of the nineteenth century, the first socialist trade unions were established. In 1902, the Chamber of Labour and, in Catholic circles, the Cantonal Circle for Political and Social Studies were formed.
The appeal of Rerum Novarum by Leone XIII, in 1891, had initially left the Catholic world of Ticino indifferent. Thanks to the initiative of don Carlo Roggero, the first Catholic Workers' Leagues spread, particularly in the Locarnese and Bellinzonese areas. In Locarno, in 1906, a permanent secretariat was established; the Bollettino del Bureau Popolare became La Gazzetta del Lavoratore the following year.
The First World War worsened workers' conditions throughout Switzerland. In November 1918, there was a three-day general strike in the main Swiss centers. A group of Christian-social workers was formed in Bellinzona. In 1919, the Federation of Christian-Social Trade Unions was founded; on May 18, OCST was officially established in Ticino. The statutes were adopted on November 16 in Bellinzona. Il Lavoro began in 1920 and ceased in 1927.
Don Luigi Del Pietro became secretary on September 1, 1929, after the bishop of Lugano, Mons. Aurelio Bacciarini, decided to entrust the union to him. Inspired by the social teaching of the Church, he relaunched OCST despite the hostility of socialist trade unions, part of the employers and respectable society. In 1933, he resumed Il Lavoro and opened the Casa del Popola in Lugano. By the end of the 1930s, OCST had matched the Chamber of Labour in membership and later became the most representative trade union in Ticino. Del Pietro's death in 1977 led to internal restructuring. ## The link with cross-border work ### What emerges for the cross-border worker The link with cross-border work appears in a specific passage: during the years of the economic boom, OCST was at the forefront of protecting foreign workers and significantly increased its membership, also thanks to the unionization of many cross-border workers. For a cross-border worker, this is the key point to retain: their presence becomes part of the history of the union within the growth of employment in Ticino and the services that OCST consolidated.
The economic context described by the source helps put that passage in perspective without separating it from the rest of the labor market. In the 1950s and until the beginning of the 1970s, construction, tourism and services expanded, while major hydroelectric projects and new roads accompanied the Canton of Ticino's entry into modernity. People from Ticino entered mainly the tertiary sector, while immigrants entered the secondary sector. With the abundance of jobs, union activity lost some of its vitality, but contributed to building the welfare state.
| Passage | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Economic boom | Expansion of construction, tourism, services and hydroelectric works | | Collective protection | Widespread collective agreements in many professions | | Crisis 1973-76 | Increase in unemployment, largely exported to foreign workers | | 1980s | Potential for a new cross-border reality, together with new pockets of poverty |
This sequence makes it possible to distinguish the collective dimension from the individual one. The source discusses the protection of foreign workers, collective agreements, services and regional offices; it does not describe an individual dispute, a payslip or a procedure for obtaining a benefit. Therefore, the cross-border worker can understand the historical role of union representation, but not get a personal answer about a contractual situation.
The text contains no information about G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates or double taxation. There are no references to INPS, the Brogeda border crossing or any possible new 2026 tax agreement. For these matters, the page is not the appropriate source; its contribution remains a reconstruction of the time when the union engaged with foreign and cross-border workers. ## How to read the history operationally ### Four steps for orientation To use the reconstruction correctly, it is advisable to follow a simple procedure: read the steps in order, distinguish the forms of organization, and stick to the data actually provided. The source recounts the historical evolution of OCST and work in Ticino; it does not provide an individual procedure for cross-border workers.
1. Start with the economy. Situate workers' societies in the agricultural Ticino of the mid-nineteenth century and use 1882, the year of the Gotthard railway, as a turning point toward factories, tourism and services.
2. Distinguish the actors. Separate the associations promoted by Italian immigrants and emigrated Ticinese, the socialist trade unions, the Catholic Workers' Leagues and OCST.
3. Follow representation. Relate collective agreements, protection for foreign workers, services and regional offices to the unionization of many cross-border workers during the boom.
4. Respect the scope. Do not turn the reconstruction into an answer about an individual employment relationship: the text provides no amounts, forms or administrative instructions.
Places also help verify the sequence. The Locarnese and Bellinzonese indicate the area of the first Catholic Workers' Leagues; Locarno hosted the permanent secretariat; Bellinzona was the site of the first Christian-social group and the adoption of the statutes. Lugano enters the trajectory with Casa del Popola and the headquarters at via Balestra 19, inaugurated in 1971.
The dates in the source are historical references, not operational deadlines. The reader can use them to distinguish the emergence of associations, the foundation of OCST, the relaunch phase under Del Pietro and the subsequent restructuring. For a cross-border worker, the most concrete point remains the one indicated by the source: during the economic boom, many workers from across the border became unionized through OCST. item.title: Generic drugs: how much more does Switzerland pay
item.description: Ten generic drugs: 241,56 francs in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Ten generics: 241,56 francs in Switzerland. - One month costs 2,9 times the average of the three neighboring countries. - Metformin: 10,85 francs in Ticino versus 1,39 in Austria. - ECB exchange rate: 1 euro = 0,9359 francs on October 6, 2026.
## Key facts Sample → ten generic drugs for everyday use. Quantity → 30 tablets for one month of treatment. Switzerland → 241,56 francs. Germany → 118 francs. Italy → 76 francs. Austria → 55 francs. Difference → from 1.8 times for candesartan to 4.6 times for metformin. Exchange rate → 1 euro = 0,9359 francs, according to the ECB exchange rate of October 6, 2026.
Ten active ingredients, four markets and a simple criterion: thirty tablets for each monthly treatment. The comparison places Switzerland, Germany, Italy and Austria side by side, using the cheapest generic available for ten everyday medicines. These are products used to treat cholesterol, high blood pressure, heartburn, diabetes, depression or to prevent heart attacks and strokes.
Same active ingredient, same dosage and, often, the same manufacturer. The selection uses the cheapest generic on the market and the retail list price, including VAT. The Swiss basket comes to 241,56 francs; the German one to 118 francs, the Italian one to 76 and the Austrian one to 55.
### The cases that shift the total
Metformin is the clearest case. For the cheapest generic, a pharmacy in Ticino charges 10,85 francs for a pack of 30 tablets. In Austria, the health insurance fund pays the equivalent of 1,39 francs, including VAT, an amount eight times lower. In Italy, by contrast, the equivalent pack costs 2,23 euros.
Atorvastatin also maintains a wide gap. The cheapest generic costs 30,25 francs in Switzerland; in Como, the equivalent pack costs 7,96 euros, approximately 7,45 francs. In Germany the price is 13,33 euros, while in Austria the health insurance fund reimburses 5,10 euros plus VAT.
The comparison also produces a paradox: the Swiss generic may cost more than the original sold across the border. Sanofi’s original Plavix costs 17,07 euros in Italy, approximately 16 francs; the cheapest generic clopidogrel in Switzerland comes to 34,70 francs, more than double. In the Swiss sample, the generic costs on average, according to the median, 18% less than the branded product, but for clopidogrel the difference is almost nil and for metformin it is 20 cents.
For a cross-border commuter looking at the relationship between Italy and Canton Ticino, this is a snapshot of drug prices, not a measure of a G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal. The text compares packs, VAT and reimbursements, not administrative rules. ## Why the gap widens
The gap cannot be explained solely by the molecule. The analysis attributes it mainly to distribution margins and pricing rules that are not very competitive. To read the result correctly, however, it is necessary to separate the retail price from the ex-factory price and distinguish the list price from the amount actually reimbursed.
### List price, reimbursement and international comparison
| Comparison | Reported result | |---|---| | Swiss sample | The generic costs, at the median, 18% less than the original. | | Meierhans, November 2024 | The cheapest foreign generic accounts for an average of 39% of the Swiss price; in the United Kingdom the percentage is 16%. | | santésuisse and Interpharma, end of May 2024 | Abroad, generics are 45,3% cheaper; for biosimilars the gap is 29,9%, while for patent-protected drugs it falls to 8,9%. |
Stefan Meierhans's comparison with 15 European countries leads to the conclusion that, on average, Swiss generics cost more than twice as much. The annual analysis by santésuisse and Interpharma reaches a similar result, but uses ex-factory prices: it does not include distribution margins and taxes. The basket examined, on the other hand, uses the retail price, the one that appears on the health insurer's or patient's bill. It is this basic difference that explains why the gap may appear larger.
The Swiss basket exceeds the German one by 105%, the Italian one by 218% and the Austrian one by 336%. Even excluding VAT, which is 19% in Germany and 2,6% in Switzerland, the ratio compared with Germany remains 2,4 to 1.
Germany shows the other side of the problem. The list price of the original is much higher: 30 tablets of Crestor cost 92,81 euros, compared with 13,42 euros for generic rosuvastatin. Health insurers, however, reimburse only up to the Festbetrag; anyone who wants the branded product pays the difference. In Austria, Sortis and Plavix are not listed in the Reimbursement Code: insurers reimburse only generics.
For a cross-border commuter, the practical takeaway is not to treat a Swiss retail price, a German list price and an Austrian reimbursement as equivalent. They are three different figures, even when they concern the same therapy. ## How to redo the comparison
The comparison method can become a small checking procedure for anyone who needs to compare a price in francs with one in euros. The rule is to keep the product, quantity, taxes, and price basis constant. Without these steps, the comparison risks mixing a generic with an original or a reimbursement with a list price.
### Five steps
1. Start with the active ingredient and dosage. The original's commercial name may change from one country to another; for this reason, the reference is the substance indicated in the therapy. The comparison points out that, often, the manufacturer is also the same.
2. Set the quantity at 30 tablets. This is the unit used to represent one month of therapy and allows equivalent packages to be compared, rather than stopping at the price of a box with a different number of doses.
3. Choose the least expensive generic available in each country. The comparison cart selects, for each of the ten active ingredients, the least costly option on the market.
4. Write down the retail price and VAT. The main figure is the one that ends up on the invoice of the health insurer or patient. For Austria, it should be noted when the reference is the amount paid by the health insurer; for Germany, the list price must be distinguished from the amount covered up to the Festbetrag.
5. Bring all amounts into the same currency. The ECB exchange rate indicated by the comparison is that of October 6, 2026: 1 euro = 0.9359 francs. Only after conversion can the totals and differences between the four countries be compared.
If one also wants to verify the ratio between originals and generics, the same discipline must be maintained. The comparison considers eight originals available in all four countries: the total is 226 francs in Switzerland, 56 in Austria, 69 in Italy, and 419 in Germany. The latter figure, however, is a list price that German health insurers do not reimburse beyond the generic's fixed amount.
For a cross-border commuter comparing a therapy between Italy and Switzerland, the useful difference is therefore not merely the final number: it is important to know whether one is looking at a generic, an original, a retail price, or a reimbursement. The comparison remains readable for each individual drug as well, from the 1.8-times ratio for candesartan to 4.6 times for metformin.
To quickly redo the conversion between euros and francs, use the comparatore CHF/EUR.

## In brief - The Swiss notice period ranges from 1 to 3 months - The resignation must be in writing and delivered to the employer - The impact on the G permit and unemployment rights is critical
## Key facts - **Minimum notice period**: 1 month - Maximum notice period: 3 months (after 10 years of service) - Format: Written (registered mail recommended) - Involved entities: SECO, USTAT, INPS
The decision to leave a job in Ticino as a cross-border worker is not just a professional choice, but a legal act with concrete repercussions on taxation and social security. In Switzerland, the Code of Obligations establishes the notice periods, which start at one month for the first two years of service, rising to two months after two years and to three months after ten years of seniority with the same employer. These terms are not strictly negotiable, but they can be modified by the individual contract only in a manner more favorable to the worker, never to their detriment.
### The resignation procedure The resignation must be communicated in writing. Although the law does not mandate registered mail, it is the only certain proof of receipt. The employer is obliged to issue a work certificate (LAVS) at the end of the employment relationship, a document essential for any future employment in Switzerland. Without this certificate, the professional career in the Canton of Ticino is significantly affected. It is fundamental to verify that the certificate contains the exact end date of the relationship, the qualification performed and, if requested, the main activity. A cross-border worker who finds themselves in a situation of voluntary resignation must be aware that this choice will also influence their rights in terms of social security and taxation, particularly regarding the management of the G permit and potential registration for unemployment. ### Impact on G permit and taxation The termination of the employment relationship directly affects the validity of the G permit. If the cross-border worker does not find new employment in Ticino within a reasonable time frame, the permit may be revoked. Furthermore, voluntary resignation results in a waiting period for unemployment benefits. In Switzerland, anyone who voluntarily resigns without a valid reason recognized by law (such as unfair dismissal or a substantial modification of contractual terms) is subject to a waiting period for unemployment benefits. The duration of this waiting period varies, but it prevents immediate access to benefits managed by the SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) or the competent cantonal funds.
On the tax side, withholding tax is deducted directly by the employer. In the event of resignation, it is important to verify that the withholding is correct for the period worked. Italian cross-border workers benefit from a tax credit in Italy to avoid double taxation, regulated by the Italo-Swiss Convention of March 9, 1976. The CE section of the Italian 730 tax return is the tool for declaring income from work in Switzerland. A cross-border worker who resigns must ensure that the employment certificate and tax statements are consistent in order to correctly complete the tax return. INPS and the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) are the reference bodies for managing social security and taxation in Italy, while in Switzerland the relevant institutions are the SECO for unemployment and the USTAT for industry statutes and regulations. ### Operational checklist for resignations Before sending the cancellation letter, it is advisable to follow a structured procedure to minimize bureaucratic risks. First, check the exact contractual and legal notice period. Secondly, write the letter clearly and concisely, indicating the last date of work. Deliver the letter by registered mail with return receipt or, if possible, in person with signature of receipt. Keep a copy and proof of delivery.
After the end of the relationship, immediately request the work certificate. Check that the data is correct. If you are entitled to a holiday allowance, make sure it is paid or compensated. As far as social security is concerned, AVS (Old Age and Survivors Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance) continue to be registered, no matter where you live. If you decide to look for a job in Ticino, register with the competent employment office. On the other hand, if you return to Italy, check how the contributions paid in Switzerland affect your right to a pension through bilateral agreements.
To calculate the net impact of your resignation and estimate the taxes due, you can use our simulation tool. The calculator helps you understand how withholding tax translates into your net salary and how to manage the tax credit in Italy.

item.title: Olgiate: Living Outpost and Sentinels in the Markets
item.description: The Presidio Vivo project gets underway in Olgiate Olona Two squares host the participating markets Easily identifiable volunteers assist the Local Police Events
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Presidio Vivo project gets underway in Olgiate Olona - Two squares host the markets involved - Clearly identifiable volunteers work alongside the Local Police - Events scheduled through December
## Key facts - Project → Presidio Vivo - Locations → piazza Don Pino Ballabio and piazza Volontari della Libertà - Volunteers → Market Sentinels - Coordination → Local Police - Call for proposals → urban security - Scheduling → events through December
### A recognizable presence in the markets
Two squares in Olgiate Olona are at the center of Presidio Vivo, the new security initiative promoted by the municipal administration through participation in a regional call for proposals dedicated to urban security.
One of the project's objectives is to strengthen the monitoring and community-outreach activities already active in the area's main market areas. The markets involved are located in piazza Don Pino Ballabio, in the historic center, and in piazza Volontari della Libertà, in the Buon Gesù neighborhood.
These are places that the municipality considers important meeting points for residents, shopkeepers and visitors. The two squares host the town's markets and represent spaces where daily presence combines with commercial activities and with people visiting the town.
During market days, security is already ensured by the presence of the Olgiate Olona Local Police. The officers provide monitoring services, traffic management and support for citizens. Presidio Vivo is designed to further strengthen this work through complementary actions involving civic presence, information and awareness-raising.
The project therefore places a recognizable volunteer presence in market locations alongside the services already provided by the Local Police. Coordination remains entrusted to the Local Police, while the planned activities aim to make attention to public spaces and the needs of those who use them more visible.
Among the initiatives are the Market Sentinels: easily recognizable volunteers who will offer support in managing spaces, welcoming and guiding market-goers. Their work will always take place under the coordination of the Local Police.
The decision to involve volunteers and associations places the project in a community-oriented framework. The market is considered not only a place to shop, but also a space for interaction and presence, where welcome and guidance can complement the monitoring already provided by officers. ## Information and community policing
The information component of Presidio Vivo is also delivered through the Local Police's community help desk. The project provides for the opening of a dedicated point for citizens, where they can receive advice and information on topics related to security and the care of shared spaces.
### From scams to the care of public spaces
The Help Desk will focus on preventing scams targeting older people, road safety, respect for public spaces, and urban upkeep. These are different issues, but they are all linked to everyday life in market areas and to the possibility for citizens to engage directly with the Local Police.
The local presence will involve officers together with volunteer associations invited to participate in the initiative. Among them, the source names the Associazione Nazionale Carabinieri in Congedo di Castellanza and the Pro Loco di Olgiate Olona. The project thus aims to combine information, assistance, and collaboration with organizations already active in the community.
Presidio Vivo also stands alongside other measures adopted by the municipal administration in the area of urban security. The initiative includes the expansion of video surveillance, with a significant increase in the number of cameras operating across the area, and the strengthening of monitoring services.
The Municipality also highlights the joint work between the Local Police Commands of Olgiate Olona and Solbiate Olona. The agreement has led to an increase in joint patrols and surveillance services, giving monitoring activities an inter-municipal dimension.
Councillor for Commerce and Digitalization Fabio Longhin presented the new project as part of a strategy based on presence, prevention, and collaboration with the community.
> «Presidio Vivo adds a new element to a strategy based on presence, prevention, and collaboration with the community».
The initiatives mentioned by Longhin also include the recent Patti per la Legalità, signed with S.O.S. Italia Libera, an anti-racketeering and anti-usury association, as well as with students at the Dante Alighieri secondary school. The administration has also supported the development of Controllo del Vicinato networks, involving both citizens and the business community.
According to the approach outlined by the councillor, video surveillance, coordinated Local Police services, prevention initiatives, and neighborhood networks are different but complementary tools. The stated goal is to help build a more aware, attentive, and cohesive community, without separating monitoring from citizens' participation. ## Appointments through December
The project will be developed through a schedule of events spread over the months through December. The planned presence in the area will include Local Police officers and the volunteer organizations involved in the initiative, with activities concentrated in the spaces hosting the town markets.
### Markets as community spaces
The schedule will complement the ordinary presence of the Local Police with the activities of the Market Sentinels, welcoming market-goers and providing guidance in the areas concerned. These actions will be joined by the Neighborhood Help Desk, conceived as an information point for residents on prevention, road safety, respect for public spaces and urban decorum.
Mayor Giovanni Montano linked this phase to recognizing the role of associations and volunteers in the town’s most frequented places. The choice concerns the markets in particular, described as spaces for relationships, social interaction and everyday presence.
For the administration, increasing the safety of these places helps strengthen the sense of community and spread a shared culture of prevention. In the mayor’s view, safety depends not only on monitoring tools, but also on an attentive and engaged community.
The role assigned to shopkeepers, volunteers, associations, schools and residents is to collaborate in promoting awareness, civic-mindedness and care for shared spaces. The direction chosen by Olgiate Olona is described as community-based safety, founded on collaboration and shared responsibility.
The project’s operational follow-up is therefore linked to a visible and coordinated presence in the two market squares. On the one hand, there will be Local Police officers engaged in monitoring activities, traffic management and supporting residents; on the other, volunteers and associations will contribute to welcoming visitors, providing guidance and caring for the spaces.
The Municipality identifies the ultimate goal as strengthening the sense of safety and improving quality of life in public spaces. Presidio Vivo also intends to promote the town markets as places of social interaction, meeting and participation, through a visible, collaborative presence attentive to the needs of the community.

item.title: Como, don Giusto welcomes the Gloria shows at Teatro Nuovo
item.description: The Gloria Cinema is closed for fire-safety compliance Don Giusto offers the Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio Sunday the 18th at 16 the Barabàn-Musica Spiccia concert
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Cinema Gloria is closed for fire-safety compliance work - Father Giusto offers Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio - The Barabàn-Musica Spiccia concert on Sunday the 18th at 16:00 - The celebrated Cinema Mondays also continue
## Key facts - Space → Cinema Gloria, via Varesina - Operator → Circolo Arci Xanadù - Performance venue → Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio - Reason for closure → bringing the premises into compliance with fire-safety regulations - Reading → Palestinians are your eyes - Concert → Barabàn and Musica Spiccia, Sunday the 18th at 4 p.m. - Financial support → proceeds from the performances
### From via Varesina to Teatro Nuovo The sudden closure of the Cinema Gloria auditorium on via Varesina has moved Circolo Arci Xanadù's performances to Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio. The theater was made available by don Giusto Della Valle, parish priest of Rebbio, who accepted the request from the association responsible for managing the neighborhood's historic cinema.
The Gloria needs to be brought into compliance with fire-safety regulations and, in the meantime, the space has been closed. The parish's availability thus makes it possible to maintain the events listed in the original program, even if in a different venue from the usual one.
The evening's program includes the theatrical reading Palestinians are your eyes. The event on Sunday the 18th at 4 p.m. will instead be a folk concert featuring the Milan-based Barabàn and the Como-based Musica Spiccia. After these events, the celebrated Cinema Mondays will also continue.
The solution therefore concerns the activities already scheduled by Circolo Arci Xanadù. No new calendar is being announced, but rather the continuation of initiatives that had been organized for the Gloria and that now have a venue in the theater in Rebbio. The move makes it possible not to interrupt the events mentioned in the source during the closure of the auditorium on via Varesina.
Don Giusto's role is to provide a venue for the association's performances. His availability comes as the Gloria continues to deal with the work required to bring it into compliance with fire-safety regulations. The link between the closure and the new venue is therefore direct: on the one hand, the cinema space cannot host the activities; on the other, Teatro Nuovo is being made available so that the program can continue.
The story concerns a cultural and community organization in the Rebbio neighborhood, but also involves the city of Como, where the Gloria is a well-known venue for its activities. The announced events are the first practical follow-up to the closure: the reading, the folk concert and the continuation of Cinema Mondays are being transferred to the parish setting in Rebbio. ## Arci di Como's response
### Gianpaolo Rosso's message The availability of Teatro Nuovo was welcomed by Arci di Como. Gianpaolo Rosso, president of Arci di Como, expressed this in a statement entitled Thank you to Father Giusto Della Valle. The message presents the parish's intervention not merely as a solution for the performances, but as a sign of the relationship between the social entities present in the area.
Within the neighborhood and beyond its borders, Arci di Como sees the Parrocchia di Rebbio, Rebbio solidale, and Father Giusto Della Valle as the greatest hope for the future in times marked by selfishness, inequalities, environmental devastation, wars, and genocides.
Rosso highlights the physical proximity among the different organizations. On Via Lissi, just a few meters apart, are the parish and the headquarters of the provincial committee, together with many Arci clubs. A short distance away, on Varesina, however, is Spazio Gloria. In the statement, the president specifies that Gloria is not merely a cinema: Arci Xanadù makes it available as a common good.
This concentration of places and activities gives rise to the idea of an area capable of becoming a first example of a liberated city, without restrictive territorial boundaries. This interpretation broadens the meaning of the availability of Teatro Nuovo: support for the club is placed within a local network made up of a parish, associations, and spaces for social interaction.
The president of Arci di Como also links Father Giusto's choice to the social, political, cultural, and human development of the area. According to Rosso, this development is a shared activity and constitutes the foundation of the convergence policy also invoked by the parish priest. He adds that, if the municipality does not understand its value, Arci will act more forcefully.
In the section devoted to the closure, Rosso speaks of a very serious blow inflicted by the paper rituals of an oppressive bureaucracy. He distinguishes this matter from the issue of safety and states that safety at Gloria was, is, and will always be guaranteed. The availability of Teatro Nuovo is therefore described as generous, timely, and lifesaving for the club.
The statement concludes with a further thank-you addressed to Father Giusto, the parish, Rebbio solidale, and the many groups that find in the oratory spaces for social interaction and incubators of generative political activities. Rosso considers these places a common heritage, not property, and defines the theater's offer as the latest gesture of solidarity, or rather of sharing. ## The expenses and the Gloria mon amour campaign
### Sinistra Italiana's appeal The economic issue is explicit. The proceeds from the shows are essential for Circolo Arci Xanadù, because they make it possible to raise the resources needed to complete the code-compliance work on the Gloria and to ensure that those who work there are paid. The closure of the venue therefore also interrupts the income linked to the activities held in the hall.
On this point, Sinistra Italiana Como spoke out, expressing its closeness to Circolo Arci Xanadù over the closure of Spazio Gloria. The statement refers to adaptation works that had already been scheduled but not yet completed. The Gloria is described as a point of reference for associations in Como and, because of the richness and originality of its cultural offerings, as an important space for social interaction and the dissemination of culture for the neighborhood and the city of Como.
Sinistra Italiana's position concerns above all the decision to impose the closure when the final works were already planned. The statement says it is difficult to understand how, after adaptation works that had dragged on over time despite economic difficulties, such a serious measure was adopted precisely when the final works had already been scheduled.
The appeal is addressed to supporters and the public. Sinistra Italiana asks people to contribute, each according to their means, to covering the expenses that the association will have to face in the absence of revenue. The costs mentioned include salaries and rents, in addition to the expenses for completing the adaptation works.
The fundraising is linked to the Gloria mon amour campaign. The statement points out that several Sinistra Italiana activists have already contributed and also invites other supporters and citizens to take part. The message therefore does not separate the defense of the cultural space from the problem of the resources needed by the association.
The follow-up described by the source unfolds on two fronts. On the one hand, Teatro Nuovo's availability makes it possible to host the scheduled shows and keep the initiatives on the program active. On the other hand, Arci Xanadù must cover current expenses and those related to completing the Gloria's code-compliance work.
The reactions of Arci di Como and Sinistra Italiana Como converge on the local value of the space and the need to support its activities. The former emphasizes the solidarity of the parish and Rebbio solidale; the latter highlights the Gloria mon amour campaign and the expenses for salaries, rents and works. These are the developments indicated by the source after the closure of the hall on via Varesina.

item.title: Varese: the stadium forecourt is named after Anastasi
item.description: The Franco Ossola forecourt bears the name of Pietro Anastasi The plaque was installed by the Municipality The naming was approved unanimously In Masnago
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Franco Ossola forecourt bears the name of Pietro Anastasi - The plaque was installed by the Municipality - The naming was approved unanimously - In Masnago, the tribute brought together teammates and supporters
## Key facts - Location → square in front of Franco Ossola Stadium - Honoree → Pietro Anastasi - Choice → dedication approved unanimously - Origin → Catania - Plaque → recalls Anastasi's rise as a champion in Varese and the memory Italy has preserved of him - Remembered figures → Ambrogio Borghi, Gedeone Carmignani and Roberto Bettega - National team → 1968 European Championship final in Rome
### The ceremony in Masnago
The square in front of Franco Ossola Stadium, in Masnago, now bears the name of Pietro Anastasi. The tribute took place in front of what had been his home as an athlete and celebrated one of the most representative figures in Varese sports and Varese Calcio. The dedication honors not only the champion but also the man, remembered as generous, humble and unforgettable.
The red-and-white roses were in Mrs. Anna's hands. Emotion could be heard in Gianluca's voice, while those who, over the course of his life and career, had known, loved and cheered for Pietro Anastasi gathered in the square. The moment brought together the memory of the goalscorer and that of the man appreciated by those who had come to Masnago for the occasion.
The decision to dedicate the area to him was described as right, deserved and appreciated, as well as approved unanimously. The Municipality installed the plaque bearing a dedication to Anastasi. The image depicts him in the red-and-white jersey as he looks toward the entrance to the Franco Ossola. The marker placed in front of the stadium thus makes the square's naming and its connection with the facility that was his home as an athlete visible.
Anastasi was born far away from here, in Catania. Yet it was precisely in Varese that he grew up, made his name and returned to live after appearing on the major stages of Italian and international football. His journey therefore connects his Catanian origins with the relationship he built with Varese, without separating his sporting career from the life he lived after returning.
For this reason, the name on the square brings together in one place the stadium, Varese Calcio and the memory of Pietro Anastasi. The ceremony gathered the affection of those who were present in person or in spirit and gave the recognition a dimension tied to the city as well as to sport. Anastasi's name is thus placed right in front of the stadium entrance, identified as the place of his experience as an athlete, within a ceremony designed to remember the champion and the man together. ## The memories of those who knew him
### A symbol for Varese
Ambrogio Borghi, who was Anastasi's teammate, summed up in the shortest and most incisive phrase of the day the meaning of the bond between the footballer and Varese.
> “If Naples has Maradona, Varese has Anastasi”
For Borghi, Anastasi's time with the red-and-white side was relatively brief, but it marked an era and linked him to the finest and strongest Varese team of all time. The phrase sums up the weight the player had in the city's sporting history, even beyond the length of his time wearing the red-and-white shirt.
Gedeone Carmignani focused above all on the striker's qualities. In his assessment, Anastasi knew how to move into space, had a nose for goal and was willing to press. With these qualities, he would be useful to every coach today. The assessment portrays a player capable of combining a presence in the box with a willingness to work even without the ball, as recalled during the meeting in Masnago.
The group of guests also used words tied to the personal dimension of the remembrance. Generous, always present and modest were the adjectives used to describe a man who was always there when someone sought him out. In this image, Pietro is not only the goalscorer celebrated in sporting memory, but a person to turn to and from whom to receive help. It is the human quality that accompanied the remembrance of his career.
Roberto Bettega came from Turin, linked to Anastasi by having played for Varese, Juventus and the national team. Bettega recalled the period when, upon returning to Juventus, the two were roommates. He scored immediately, then went scoreless for many matches; Anastasi stood by him, helped him, and his teammate began scoring again. The testimony brings a specific episode of personal support into the ceremony, distinct from the account of goals and jerseys worn.
The words heard in Masnago thus set the technical assessment of the striker alongside the memory of a person who was present in the lives of others. The celebration of the athlete belongs to the history of football; that of the man is conveyed instead through his relationships with teammates and those who sought him out. It is this dual reading, sporting and human, that explains the participation of the guests who came for Pietro Anastasi. ## The story told by the plaque
### From the national team to the provincial side
The Municipality has installed a plaque commemorating Anastasi's success in Varese and the memory Italy has preserved of him. The image of the footballer in a red-and-white shirt faces the entrance to the Franco Ossola. The message goes beyond Varese's history and also evokes what Anastasi represented for those who followed the national team and for those who had seen him star in the Italian championships.
For national-team supporters, the memory is tied to the 1968 European Championship final, played in Rome. Anastasi and Gigi Riva scored the two goals of the match. For those who had followed Varese, on the other hand, his name evoked the season of the provincial side capable of upending the league's balance, with the 5-0 victory over Juventus. Inter came after Juventus, but the bond with the red-and-white shirt remained the focal point of the dedication in front of the stadium.
### The decisive move to Varese
The plaque also speaks to those who, having emigrated from the South, looked to a footballer as an example, an idol and a reason for redemption. Anastasi, born in Catania and later raised in Varese, became a symbol for different audiences: for those who supported Italy, for those who recognized the strength of the provincial side and for those who supported the player at the big clubs.
The origins of his relationship with Varese are conveyed through Guido Borghi's account and an incident involving Alfredo Casati, a club executive. Casati was supposed to board a flight in Catania, but gave his seat on the plane to a woman who urgently needed to return to Milan. He therefore stayed in the city and took the opportunity to attend a match. Massiminiana were playing: Casati saw Anastasi and decided to bring him to Varese.
From that decision developed Pietro's deep bond with the new city, with his Anna and with so many people. The account of the transfer adds a concrete element to the ceremony: before the champion celebrated by the national team and the big clubs, there was the player seen on the pitch in Catania. Fate, as the account heard in Masnago described it, brought that match, Casati and his future experience in Varese together.
It is this sequence that completes the meaning of the square's new name. In front of the Franco Ossola, the athlete remembered for his goals, the man described as generous and the person who had built a relationship with Anna and the city came together. The applause directed at Anastasi, whether in person or in thought, accompanied a dedication born of his sporting history and his life in Varese.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/se-napoli-ha-maradona-varese-ha-anastasi-il-piazzale-dello-stadio-intitolato-a-pietruzzu/2708932/)*

item.title: Gazzada Schianno: sport and solidarity event on October 25
item.description: Sunday, October 25, 2026 sports and solidarity at Gazzada Schianno The event is scheduled from 14:30 to 19:30 AGIFAR Varese organizes with the doctor
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Sunday, October 25, 2026: sport and solidarity in Gazzada Schianno - The event is scheduled from 14:30 to 19:30 - AGIFAR Varese is organizing it with Dr. Nathalie Biasolo - The fee is 30 euros and supports the project
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Event | «A Kick to Cocaine – Sport, well-being and solidarity» | | Where | SMASH Bellavista Center, Località Campagnola | | When | Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 14:30 to 19:30 | | Promotion | AGIFAR Varese, with Nathalie Biasolo | | Activities | Football fitness, five-a-side football and yoga | | Participants | Citizens, families and sports enthusiasts | | Fee | 30 euros per person | | Proceeds | Entirely allocated to developing the project |
### The initiative in Gazzada Schianno
Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 14:30 to 19:30, Smash Bellavista in Gazzada Schianno will host «A Kick to Cocaine – Sport, well-being and solidarity», a charitable initiative against addictions promoted by AGIFAR Varese. The specified venue is Bellavista Società Polisportiva Dil. Srl, in Località Campagnola.
Movement, prevention and social inclusion characterize the event. AGIFAR Varese (Association of Young Pharmacists of the province of Varese) organizes it with Dr Nathalie Biasolo, who practices medicine and works as a sports physiologist.
The «A Kick to Cocaine» project is the core of the proposal and aims to combat and prevent addictions through football fitness, a group discipline inspired by football, and team sports. From this perspective, team sports are presented as an opportunity to create positive connections, support inclusion and promote the psychological and physical well-being of young people.
The initiative is open to citizens, families and sports enthusiasts. Anyone who simply wants to learn about the project and take part in the social gathering may also participate. You do not need to be an athlete: the individual sporting activities are optional.
The afternoon is therefore designed with a format not reserved for those who already practice sports. Participation combines a presentation, different activities and a final sharing moment, allowing those present to choose whether to join the scheduled sports sessions.
The schedule combines football fitness, five-a-side football and yoga with the presentation of the project and the shared aperitif dinner. Participation does not require being an athlete, because each sporting activity is optional. The social gathering is scheduled for the final part of the afternoon. ## The project and the local network
The «A Kick to Cocaine» project was developed with the support of lecturers and researchers from Syddansk Universitet, the University of Southern Denmark. The presentation scheduled in the program also covers the international pathway linked to the initiative and will take place in the panoramic room.
### Team sports and prevention
Football fitness is described as a group activity inspired by football. This practice is complemented by team sports, offered to young people as an opportunity to build positive relationships, support inclusion and promote physical and mental well-being. The project aims to combat and prevent addictions through these activities, bringing the subject of prevention into a collective movement experience.
The connection with public health is also indicated by the mission of AGIFAR Varese, which promotes educational and social initiatives in addition to bringing together young pharmacists in the area.
### The role of AGIFAR Varese
Founded in 2023, AGIFAR Varese brings together young pharmacists in the area and promotes educational and social initiatives to protect public health. For the event in Gazzada Schianno, the association is collaborating with Dr. Nathalie Biasolo, a physician and sports physiologist, who will lead the football fitness session.
The initiative is held under the patronage of the Order of Pharmacists of the Province of Varese and Federfarma Varese. Otofarma, Ikigai Beauty and SV Integratori are also listed as sponsors. The support and patronage accompany a project that brings together the work of young pharmacists, sports practice and the pathway developed with the Danish university.
The day does not end with the sporting activity: the program also includes a presentation of the project and a social gathering, elements listed alongside the movement sessions. ## The day's schedule
### From registration to apericena
The schedule is divided between welcome, presentation, sports activities, a break and a social gathering. The timetable indicated by the organizers is as follows:
| Time | Activity |\n|---|---|\n| 14:30–15:00 | Welcome and participant registration |\n| 15:00–15:30 | In the panoramic room: presentation of the «A Kick to Cocaine» project and its international journey |\n| 15:30–16:30 | Football fitness session led by Dr Nathalie Biasolo |\n| 15:30–17:30 | Five-a-side football tournament taking place simultaneously on the grass field |\n| 16:30–17:30 | Yoga class with Lisa |\n| 17:30–18:15 | Time for showers and changing |\n| 18:15 | Awards for the winning team and the most athletic participants |\n| 18:30 | Apericena together and closing farewells by 19:30 |
Registration opens the afternoon, while the presentation in the panoramic room precedes the start of the sports activities. Football fitness and the five-a-side tournament start at 15:30, according to two different time slots.
Anyone arriving without a team will be assigned to groups by the organizers. For the yoga session with Lisa, it is advisable to bring a mat. Once the sports activities have ended, time will be available for showers and changing.
At 18:15, awards will be presented to the winning team and the most athletic participants. At 18:30, the shared apericena and final farewells begin, with closing by 19:30.
Participation requires advance registration by completing the online form and indicating any food intolerances or allergies. The fee is 30 euros per person, including the apericena and all optional sports activities. All proceeds will be donated to support the development of the project.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/a-kick-to-cocaine-a-gazzada-schianno-un-pomeriggio-tra-sport-benessere-e-solidarieta-con-agifar-varese/2709493/)*

item.description: OCST offers assistance with employment, payslips and taxation The Cross-Border Workers Office handles tax law and social security AVS, LADI and LPP are included
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - OCST provides assistance with employment, payslips and taxation - The Cross-Border Workers Office handles tax law and social security - AVS, LADI and LPP are covered by the advisory service - The offers involve a form, code, card or insurer
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Services | provided according to specific regulations | | Areas | labour, payroll, social insurance and taxation | | Cross-border workers' office | cross-border tax law and social security | | Offices | Chiasso, Mendrisio, Bioggio, Locarno and Lugano | | Patronato offices | INAS and ACLI, affiliated with OCST | | Information | meetings, «il Lavoro», website, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn | | Vehicles | 10% on labour costs with a replacement vehicle | | MUSEC | admission for 10 CHF instead of 15 CHF |
OCST services are provided according to specific regulations. The page dedicated to the association presents a range of services that, for cross-border workers, begins with the employment relationship and extends to cross-border tax and social issues.
For cross-border workers, the list brings together workplace support, social information and benefits reserved for female and male OCST members.
### The scope of assistance
The first level is legal assistance and/or advice. It concerns issues relating to the employment relationship and payroll, but also includes the social insurance schemes AVS, AI, LADI and LPP. The same area covers illness and accidents, family allowances, taxation and tenancy. For a cross-border worker, the list therefore brings together several areas of advice.
Support is provided for strike actions, as are contributions for training. Access to these services is governed by specific regulations, which members must consult to verify the conditions.
### The Cross-Border Workers' Office
Assistance for cross-border workers includes advice and information on cross-border tax law, social security, occupational pensions, social insurance, work permits, family allowances and unemployment benefits. The services also include coverage, at the member’s expense, of the costs of emergency hospitalisation in the event of illness and free membership in CISL.
This support is complemented by the presence of patronato offices: INAS operates at the OCST offices in Chiasso, Mendrisio, Bioggio and Locarno, while ACLI is present at the Lugano office. Both are affiliated with the trade union.
The picture is completed by regular information meetings, the newspaper «il Lavoro», the OCST website, the current-affairs newsletter and the Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn channels. For special offers, the procedure differs: in some cases, a form must be requested via the form; in others, the possibility must be reported to one’s insurer. This distinction, already indicated on the page, determines the first step for using the benefit. For a cross-border worker affiliated with OCST, the practical value of the benefits depends on the channel specified for obtaining them. The page alternates among a form, notification to one's insurer, a card and a promotional code. This distinction prevents treating a discount as automatic when it instead requires a specific step.
### One method for each offer
| Method | Source indication | |---|---| | Form | Request the form for special offers | | Insurer | Inform one's insurer of the possibility | | OCST card | Present it for the indicated benefits | | Code | «OCST» for Masa Coffee; OCST promotional code for the account |
In the insurance sector, a 10% discount is indicated on private liability, household contents, building insurance and motor vehicle insurance, along with a free pension analysis and personalized advice. This is followed by 10% off selected supplementary insurance policies and 9% off some complementary insurance policies. For labor, 10% off is indicated, with a replacement vehicle included throughout Switzerland; for work covered by insurance, a voucher of 250 fr. toward the contractual deductible is mentioned; the «Prendi e vai» subscription provides 20%, not combinable.
In the travel sector, the source lists 15€ for flights, 20€ for hotels, 40€ for the flight+hotel combination and 4% on gift cards. At MUSEC in Lugano, admission is 10 CHF rather than 15 CHF, with 20% off selected bookshop items.
### Conditions to read
Among the establishments, Old Wild West in Mendrisio indicates 15% off the total bill, not combinable with other promotions; Pizzarella-Burgerella applies 10% on site, with no home delivery, while for home delivery it indicates a complimentary drink per order. Brico SA, Ristorante Elvezia 31 and Pescheria Lawrence indicate 10% upon presentation of the OCST card.
For the bank account, opening is 100% online with the OCST promotional code through the OCST contact person; the source also indicates no fee linked to residence abroad. The list includes five years of package fees free, one free year on Mastercard silver and, in another entry, one year free on packages. The 20% «Prendi e vai» and Old Wild West's 15% cannot be combined. The operating procedure starts with the subject matter and ends with the channel indicated for the benefit. To avoid unforeseen steps, the member can follow a sequence based on the methods described on the page.
### 1. Identify the service
The first choice is to distinguish legal advice from the commercial agreement. For issues concerning employment relationships, payslips, AVS, AI, LADI, LPP, illness, accidents, family allowances, taxation or tenancy, the page places the matter under legal and juridical assistance and/or advice. If the issue concerns cross-border tax law, social security, occupational pension provision, work permits or unemployment benefits, the indicated reference is the Cross-Border Workers' Office. Subsidies for strike action and training contributions are among the listed services and follow specific regulations.
### 2. Submit the correct request
For special offers, use the form to request the application form. The page indicates this in several places, so the form is the step to follow when the agreement requires it. For insurance coverage, the indicated procedure is different: notify your insurer of the possibility. The channel specified by the offer should not be replaced with a generic one.
### 3. Apply the card or code
For Brico SA, Ristorante Elvezia 31, Old Wild West di Mendrisio, Pizzarella-Burgerella and Pescheria Lawrence, the source indicates presenting the OCST card. For Masa Coffee, the discount code is «OCST». For the bank account, the OCST promotional code is available from the OCST contact person; opening takes place 100% online through the CA and OCST - Corporate partner offer. These are different operating methods and must be kept separate.
### 4. Check timing and access points
For the admission ticket, the indicated condition is a 15% discount until December 23 and 20% on Tuesdays, for OCST members and three accompanying persons. For an assistance case, the local contacts are Patronato INAS at the OCST offices in Chiasso, Mendrisio, Bioggio and Locarno, and Patronato ACLI at the Lugano office. To stay up to date, the page lists periodic meetings, «il Lavoro», the website, newsletter, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn.
The same criterion applies to the other benefits: the cross-border worker can consult the specific offer before choosing whether to request the form or use the code. The source links each benefit to the relevant partner and the indicated method. For taxation and payslips, find out more with calcolatore fiscale.

## TL;DR - Arrested a 26-year-old Russian citizen - The glass window of a garage was damaged - Attempted escape after being detained - Como prison pending immediate trial
## Key facts - What → unauthorized entry into the Fire Brigade headquarters - Where → via Valleggio, Como - When → Wednesday afternoon, around 15.00 - Who → 26-year-old Russian citizen - Outcome → transfer to Como prison
Yesterday afternoon, Wednesday, the Como State Police arrested a 26-year-old Russian citizen with no fixed address in Italy and irregular status in the country. The man had unlawfully entered the headquarters of the Fire Brigade Command on via Valleggio, in Como. The report also mentions some damage, including the glass window of a garage.
### The report and initial response
Around 15.00, officers from the police headquarters patrol unit arrived at the Fire Brigade Command headquarters after being informed that someone was inside the facility. Before the police arrived, the personnel on site had restrained the 26-year-old following the damage. The patrol then took custody of the man, who was found to be agitated.
During a personal search, the Russian citizen immediately showed little cooperation. He then had an outburst of anger in the service vehicle and attempted to escape. The officers promptly restrained him. The sequence described therefore begins with the unauthorized presence at the headquarters, continues with the reported damage, and culminates in the attempt to evade control after being detained.
The initial response took place entirely in Como and involved the headquarters on via Valleggio, Fire Brigade personnel and officers from the police headquarters patrol unit. At this stage, the source places the unauthorized entry, the damaged glass window and the attempted escape before the further checks carried out by the State Police. ## Checks at Police Headquarters
### Identification and behavior
The attempted escape did not result in the man getting away. In an attempt to break free from the officers, the 26-year-old kicked and punched one of the officers. The officers restrained him and then took him to Police Headquarters for fingerprint and photographic identification checks and the customary checks.
The checks uncovered several aliases, as well as various offenses related to immigration regulations and offenses against public administration, in addition to criminal convictions. The identification therefore added to the elements of the intervention the results of the checks carried out in the Police Headquarters offices.
Even while in the holding cells, the detainee maintained an aggressive attitude. This behavior was observed while he was still in police custody, before medical personnel intervened.
Because the 26-year-old was highly agitated, the officers called in medical personnel. The request was made while the 26-year-old was in the holding cells.
The part of the incident following his being taken into custody therefore includes physical contact with one of the officers, the restraint, being taken to Police Headquarters, and the carrying out of the checks. During the same period, the aliases coming to light, the offenses indicated, the criminal convictions reported in the account, and the aggressive behavior that led to the request for medical assistance all occurred. The checks and the time spent in the holding cells are described before the medical intervention.
The detainee's time at Police Headquarters therefore had a dual purpose: identification, through fingerprint and photographic checks, and management of the detainee, because of the attitude he maintained in the holding cells. ## The arrest and the wait for the fast-track trial
### The charges
The medical staff, responding at the officers' request, calmed the 26-year-old and transported him to a hospital. Following this, the Russian citizen was arrested.
The report cites as grounds for the arrest aggravated property damage, violence, threats, resistance and injury to a public official, disruption of a public service, defacement and unlawful entry, as well as resistance to a public official. The list brings together the offenses reported by Como State Police concerning the incident that took place at the Fire Brigade headquarters.
The wording includes aggravated property damage; in the reconstruction of the intervention, the garage's glass window is mentioned among the damage. Unlawful entry, disruption of a public service and defacement are also listed, together with the charges of violence, threats, resistance and injury to a public official and resistance to a public official.
### Custody in Como
By order of the judicial authority, the 26-year-old was committed to Como prison. This committal came after the transfer to hospital and after the arrest for the offenses listed in the report. The destination indicated is therefore Como prison, where the man was transferred while awaiting the fast-track trial.
The final sequence reported is that of the medical intervention, the arrest and the subsequent order of the judicial authority. The follow-up indicated by the source is awaiting the fast-track trial and the arrested man's remaining in Como prison. Como prison is therefore where the 26-year-old was committed after the order of the judicial authority, while the fast-track trial remains the proceeding awaited at the stage described.

item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - SSR cuts another 202 full-time positions - 173 reductions concern the Operations sector - The measure enables savings of 41 million francs - Around 270 million francs in savings are needed by 2029
Total cuts → 202 full-time positions Operations sector → 173 positions Other sectors → 29 positions Savings from the measure → 41 million francs 2027 target → 80 million francs 2029 target → around 270 million francs RSI → up to 12 fewer positions in 2027
SSR announced on Thursday the elimination of another 202 full-time jobs. The decision includes 173 cuts in Operations. The other 29 positions concern Human Resources, Finance, Communication & Public Affairs and Staff.
The measure will enable Società svizzera di radiotelevisione to save 41 million francs. The measure is part of recent political decisions, including the reduction of the license fee to 300 francs. As a result of these choices, the company is required to save around 270 million by 2029, of which 80 million already in 2027. The figure of 41 million concerns this measure, while the other amounts indicate overall targets over different time horizons.
### The section on 2027 With the measures announced last month for the regional units RSI, RTR, RTS and SRF, SSR says it has fully realized the savings planned for 2027. For RSI, the figure indicated is a reduction of up to 12 positions in 2027. The source does not specify the distribution of the positions among locations, functions or categories of workers.
The categories do not have the same numerical weight: 173 positions are concentrated in Operations, while 29 are distributed among the four areas listed. The text does not provide an internal breakdown of the 29 and does not assign the 202 to individual locations. The overall figure refers to full-time jobs, without a list of people or duties involved.
Personnel management will, where possible, rely on natural turnover and retirements. According to SSR, this approach will absorb around half of the reductions in Operations and support sectors. However, it will not be enough to avoid all the effects: layoffs and early retirements are described as inevitable. The company will apply its social plan.
For those who live near the border and work in Ticino, the verifiable fact is therefore a reorganization that also includes RSI; it is not possible, however, to determine from the source how many cross-border workers are involved or which individual conditions will change. The text stops at the overall numbers, company areas and timing of the savings. ## For the cross-border worker, the actual scope of the news
A cross-border worker who works for SSR, or is considering a job connected with RSI, can use the news to identify organizational risk, not to automatically calculate a change in their paycheck. The text refers to positions being eliminated, savings and personnel management; it does not indicate salaries, working hours, locations, individual contracts or criteria for choosing the people affected. The overall figure of 202 therefore cannot be turned into a figure for cross-border workers.
The first comparison concerns the areas: 173 positions are in Operations, 29 in support sectors. A role falling within one of these areas is not described as automatically eliminated. The source does not provide a list of functions, nor does it distinguish between employees residing in Switzerland and cross-border workers. The RSI figure is also phrased as up to 12 fewer positions in 2027: it is not a description of individual positions and contains no names or locations.
For readers in Canton Ticino, the practical angle therefore remains employment-related. The source does not announce changes to the G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal. It does not address tax rebates, withholding tax, INPS, Brogeda or double taxation. These elements cannot be inferred from SSR's savings plan, because the text does not link them to the reorganization.
The difference between natural attrition and imposed departures is the second point to consider. SSR states that natural turnover and retirements will cover, as far as possible, about half of the reductions in the sectors indicated. It adds, however, that dismissals and early retirements are unavoidable and that the social plan will be applied. Without details about the plan, it is not possible to calculate compensation, timelines or conditions for an individual cross-border worker.
The timetable has two levels: 80 million in savings already in 2027 and around 270 million by 2029. These are company targets, not individual deadlines. The source does not indicate dates for personal communications, nor a different procedure for those crossing the border. The cross-border worker cannot infer from these figures an automatic change in their permit, social security or taxation.
The before-and-after comparison is therefore limited: the source does not provide a previous snapshot of the number of employees by area, but it discloses the overall volume of the cuts, the main breakdown and the savings horizon. The figure serves to clarify the direction of the reorganization, not to anticipate the outcome of every employment relationship. ## How to use the information
The source does not describe an individual procedure for employees or indicate forms, offices or personal deadlines. To avoid conflating company data with personal circumstances, a worker can follow a five-step reading, all based on the published information.
1. Separate the scope. Note that the measure concerns 202 full-time positions and that the largest share, 173, is in Operations. The remaining 29 are associated with the four areas listed: Human Resources, Finance, Communications & Public Affairs and Staff.
2. Isolate the RSI figure. Note separately the wording up to 12 fewer positions in 2027. That “up to” indicates a threshold reported by the source; it does not justify turning it into a certain number of people or a list of roles.
3. Separate the timelines. 2027 is the time horizon for the first 80 million in savings and for the measures already implemented for the regional units; 2029 is the deadline indicated for approximately 270 million. These are two distinct company references.
4. Distinguish the methods. Note that natural attrition and retirements absorb, as far as possible, about half of the reductions in Operations and the support sectors. However, the same communication points to unavoidable layoffs and early retirements and the implementation of the social plan.
5. Stop at the available data. The text does not provide individual criteria, departure dates, social plan amounts, locations or names. It therefore does not make it possible to calculate the personal impact for a cross-border worker, or to infer effects on withholding tax, AVS or other institutions not mentioned.
For those who work across the border, this method avoids two opposite errors: reading the 202 positions as if they were all in RSI, or treating the up to 12 RSI positions as a list of names. The source makes it possible to follow the scope of the savings and the stated methods, but it does not contain an individual communication from the company. Since no personal forms, offices or deadlines are indicated, adding them would mean going beyond the available data.

## TL;DR - Three arrests in Mendrisiotto - Suspected scams involving shock calls - Vehicle with Czech license plates found in Chiasso - A second afternoon scam was foiled
## Key facts - Who: two Slovaks aged 39 and 28, and a 30-year-old Czech - When: last Wednesday; scam reported on September 21 - Where: Mendrisiotto, Chiasso and Melano - What: cash and valuables found in the vehicle
### From the report to the discovery
Three men were arrested in the Mendrisiotto last Wednesday: two Slovaks aged 39 and 28 and a 30-year-old Czech, all residing in their respective countries of origin. The three are suspected of having participated in scams targeting elderly people through the so-called “shock calls.”
The victim’s relatives triggered the investigation into a scam that took place on September 21. The report led to work by the cantonal police and the Lugano police, ultimately resulting in the identification of a vehicle with Czech license plates.
On Wednesday, in Chiasso, staff from the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security located the trio’s vehicle, finding cash and valuables inside.
The three are suspected of having committed a scam that morning in Melano. Another one, already planned for the afternoon, was thwarted. Their possible involvement in other similar incidents remains to be verified. ## What has been established and what remains open
The news report distinguishes between what has been reported based on the findings and what still needs to be verified. The arrests, the presence of the vehicle with Czech license plates in Chiasso, and the discovery of cash and valuables are elements reported in the reconstruction. What remains under verification, however, is both the possible involvement of the three in other similar incidents and the full picture of the suspected scams.
The term «suspects» defines the level of information available: the source attributes possible involvement to the three and reports a suspected scam in Melano, but does not present their possible role in other cases as already verified. The second incident is likewise described as a scam planned for the afternoon and foiled, without further details.
### The connection with cross-border work
For a cross-border worker reading the news, this distinction avoids unwarranted connections. ## TL;DR - Prohibitions active from 19 October at 6.30 am to 24 October at midnight - Como-Manchester United on Wednesday 21 at 18.45 - Como-Sassuolo Saturday 24 at 3 pm - Deviated transit on the contravial towards via Puecher
## Key facts - Ordinance → n. 418 of 13 October 2026 - Area → via Vittorio Veneto, around the Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium - Parking → prohibition with forced removal - Transit → deviation towards via Puecher - Purpose → TV technical means and mobile barriers
From 19 October at 6.30am, the area of Via Vittorio Veneto in Como will be affected by temporary changes to traffic in view of two Como 1907 matches at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium. The provisions will remain in force until midnight on Saturday 24 October, with the possibility of continuing beyond that deadline if the operations related to the meetings make it necessary.
The calendar includes the UEFA Champions League match against Manchester United, set for Wednesday 21 October at 6.45pm, and the Serie A match against Sassuolo, scheduled for Saturday 24 October at 3pm. After the defeat in the Champions League, Como 1907 must therefore face a tight sequence of events, while the city prepares the stands in the stadium area.
### The section affected by the prohibitions
The parking ban will come into effect on both sides of Via Vittorio Veneto, from Largo Borgonovo to the pedestrian crossing near electricity pole number 6921. The measure provides for forced removal and also applies to vehicles with a permit for people with disabilities. The space will be used for the technical means of television filming and to install mobile barriers intended to protect the equipment.
A second ban will concern five parking spaces between electricity poles number 6925 and 6926. At that point the area must remain free to allow vehicle access to the service road.
In the same time interval, transit will be prohibited in the stretch between Largo Borgonovo and the pedestrian crossing near pole 6921. Traffic will be directed on the service road of Via Vittorio Veneto towards Via Puecher. The local police indicate the manhole and priority to pedestrians, inviting them to follow the temporary signs. Further measures are also planned for other areas and streets of the stadium, which will be published later. For cross-border commuters who need to reach the stadium area for a work trip or for an appointment, the notice should be read as a combination of different prohibitions. The provision is not limited to removing some parking spaces: it closes a section of Via Vittorio Veneto to traffic and imposes specific regulations on the service road as well. The difference is practical: leaving the car and crossing the area are two operations subject to separate rules.
### Parking and transit are not the same thing
| Situation | Rule indicated | | Stop in the wide stretch Borgonovo-palo 6921 | Ban on both sides, with forced removal | | Five places between posts 6925 and 6926 | Free area for access to the service road | | Transit in the indicated section | Vehicle ban | | Contravial towards via Puecher | Manhole and priority for pedestrians |
For those who have to organize a passage in the area, the first consequence is that it is not advisable to plan the journey counting on stopping along the main stretch. The ban covers both sides and the forced removal also eliminates the possibility of a temporary stop. The notice also explicitly includes vehicles marked for people with disabilities.
The second consequence concerns the continuation of the journey. The closed section cannot be traveled by vehicles; the indicated deviation leads to the service road in the direction of via Puecher. The passage, however, is not described as an ordinary lane: the local police ask you to proceed at walking pace and always give priority to pedestrians. For a cross-border worker who finds himself passing through that area, compliance with these conditions becomes an integral part of the deviation.
The time window includes both the day of the match against Manchester United and that of the match against Sassuolo. Furthermore, the limitations may remain operational beyond midnight on October 24th if organizational activities are not concluded. Anyone planning a trip must therefore consider the entire indicated period and any signage updates. In fact, the source recalls the possibility of other measures in further areas and streets of the stadium. Whoever needs to move in the area can transform the warning into a simple operational sequence. The steps concern date, road section, stop, detour and signs.
### Check before leaving
1. Check the period. The measures start at 6.30am on October 19th and are scheduled until midnight on October 24th. This is the window to consider before entering the area of ​​via Vittorio Veneto.
2. Identify the stretch. The main parking ban affects both sides of the segment that starts from Largo Borgonovo and arrives at the pedestrian crossing located near electricity pole number 6921. The five stalls between poles 6925 and 6926 have separate regulations and must remain free.
3. Do not leave the vehicle in prohibited areas. Forced removal accompanies the ban and also concerns vehicles with a badge for people with disabilities. The notice therefore expressly includes these vehicles among those affected by the measure.
4. Follow the planned detour. In the section where transit is prohibited, traffic is directed onto the service road of via Vittorio Veneto towards via Puecher. On the service road you will have to advance at walking pace, always giving priority to pedestrians.
5. Read the signs on site. The local police invite you to pay attention to the temporary signs, especially on the days of the two matches. Further measures have also been announced for other areas and streets of the stadium, while the limitations already foreseen may continue if it is necessary to complete the operations related to the matches.
For the border reader, the final check is concrete: check whether the movement crosses the indicated stretch, exclude parking in the affected areas and prepare to follow the service road. The notice describes a procedure focused on circulation and compliance with temporary directions.
The area will be used for the technical means of television broadcasts and for the mobile barriers necessary to protect the equipment. The signs therefore remain the reference during the set-up and during the competitions. If the operations are not completed by the deadline, the bans may continue for the required time.
